Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton.

articles.title: Week 9 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Flex, PPR Advice for Fringe Fantasy Football Stars
articles.summary: The 2026 fantasy football season has been a roller coaster thus far, and things aren't likely to slow down as midseason approaches. Injuries, unexpected slumps, and tough matchups have made it difficult to pick which fringe starters are worth playing—even in the versatile flex spot.
articles.body:
The 2026 fantasy football season has been a roller coaster thus far, and things aren't likely to slow down as midseason approaches. Injuries, unexpected slumps, and tough matchups have made it difficult to pick which fringe starters are worth playing—even in the versatile flex spot.

This week, managers must also contend with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans being on bye.

Here, you'll find early start/sit recommendations for some top fringe flex options for point-per-reception (PPR) leagues in Week 9.

Start: Quinshon Judkins, RB, Cleveland Browns

Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins had a miserable outing against the Pittsburgh Steelers last week. Cleveland fell behind early and its suspect offensive line struggled to open holes against an aggressive defensive front.

Judkins has mostly been a disappointment this season because of Cleveland's O-line issues and its tendency to play from behind. However, he tallied 23.4 fantasy points against the Tennessee Titans two weeks ago and could trend in that direction again this week.

The Browns are set to visit the New Orleans Saints, who have struggled defensively, especially against the run, this season. The Saints are coming off their bye and may have a solid plan for slowing Judkins, but it's a promising matchup overall.

New Orleans has surrendered 11 rushing touchdowns this season and has surrendered more fantasy points to opposing running backs than any other team.

Sit: Ollie Gordon II, RB, Miami Dolphins

Miami Dolphins running back Ollie Gordon II has been much more consistent than Judkins, which may be surprising to many managers. Gordon didn't even step in as Miami's lead back until De'Von Achane was lost for the season.

Over his last five games, Gordon has reached double-digit fantasy points four times.

However, Gordon hasn't knifed through every defense he has faced. He struggled to gain traction against the New England Patriots on Sunday, finishing with a modest 6.9 fantasy points. He could have another underwhelming day this week against the Detroit Lions.

The Lions have featured one of the league's worst pass defenses, but Gordon isn't heavily utilized in the passing game. Detroit also has a stout defensive front and has surrendered the fourth-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs this season.

Start: Ladd McConkey, WR, Los Angeles Chargers

Ladd McConkey has been one of fantasy's biggest letdowns this season, largely because the Los Angeles Chargers have been the biggest disappointment in the NFL.

The Chargers remain the league's only winless team, and their offense has been a mess under new coordinator Mike McDaniel. McConkey, meanwhile, has been in and out of the lineup with injuries.

Yet, McConkey has shown glimmers of hope. He has reached double-digit fantasy points three times and is coming off a 12.6-point outing with a strong matchup looming.

Los Angeles will host the Houston Texans, who have surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing wide receivers in 2026.

New York Jets receiver Garrett Wilson has been a volatile flex option in 2026. While he's been dependable more often than not—he has five double-digit outings thus far—he disappointed in Weeks 6 and 7 as rookie Omar Cooper Jr. started to shine.

Wilson rebounded in a big way against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, finishing with 6 catches on 11 targets for 83 yards and 14.3 fantasy points. Cooper was not targeted a single time.

While the Jets may try to target Wilson heavily again this week, there's no guarantee that the strategy will work or that he'll come through for fantasy managers. New York is set to visit the Kansas City Chiefs and will likely need a more varied approach to outmaneuver Steve Spagnuolo's defense.

Only the Seattle Seahawks have surrendered fewer fantasy points to opposing receivers than Kansas City.

*Fantasy scoring information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Updated Cleveland Browns Team Needs 1 Week Ahead of the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: With a little less than one week until the 2026 NFL trade deadline, the Cleveland Browns find themselves in a unique position.
articles.body:
With a little less than one week until the 2026 NFL trade deadline, the Cleveland Browns find themselves in a unique position.

The young roster has proven to be good enough to win games against bad opponents. They are in a position to be part of the playoff race down the stretch despite losing 27-6 at Pittsburgh last week.

At the same time, that loss can't be ignored. The Browns' roster has real holes that will likely need to be fixed before they can actually be considered a serious playoff team.

Whether they'll seek to patch at least one of the holes at the trade deadline is yet to be seen, but here are the five biggest needs they have going into the deadline with trade options for each.

The Browns are tied for ninth in the league in sacks with 21 on the season. Yet, they could really use another edge-rusher who can get after the quarterback.

Thus far, Jared Verse has not been the No. 1 pass-rusher the team was hoping for when he was included in the Myles Garrett trade. He has mostly been a good run defender who sets a good edge, but he has yet to notch his first sack.

Instead, the Browns have benefitted from multiple interior rushers and second-level defenders getting to the quarterback. Isaiah McGuire is the only edge-rusher with more than one sack on the season.

The Browns have two powerful rushers in Verse and McGuire; the question is whether a more speed-based, bendy rusher on the edge would make their pass rush even more dangerous.

Potential Trade Targets: Josh Sweat (Cardinals), Khalil Mack (Chargers), Jermaine Johnson II (Titans)

If there's one element of the Cleveland Browns that is most disappointing this season, it's the run game.

There's a combination of factors at play. The scheme isn't always great because they are in shotgun so much. The offensive line hasn't always cleared the most run lanes and the running back, primarily Quinshon Judkins, hasn't done much with the ball.

One trade or personnel change won't solve all the problems. But at this point, Judkins bears some of the blame. According to Player Profiler , the Browns running back ranks 48th in yards created per touch.

The blocking isn't always great, but other backs in the offense have been more efficient in smaller samples. If the Browns were to get aggressive, it would be good for them to add another power back who is going to let inside runs develop and be more reliable.

Potential Trade Targets: Tony Pollard (Titans), Tyrone Tracy (Giants), Kimani Vidal (Chargers)

Tight end might seem like a ridiculous need given Harold Fannin Jr.'s 10-catch game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, but Fannin's skills are exactly why another tight end is a need.

The Browns are 27th in 12-personnel (one running back, two tight ends) usage in the league at just 14.3 percent . That's not great for a team that is struggling to run the ball.

Adding an additional blocker on the field would not only give the Browns more opportunities in the run game, but it would also mean Fannin could be used more like a moving weapon in the pass game.

Blake Whiteheart has been serviceable, but he doesn't offer enough as a run blocker to incentivize more 12 personnel.

Adding a versatile blocking tight end would give the Browns more schematic flexibility.

Potential Trade Targets: Dallas Goedert (Eagles), Charlie Kolar (Chargers), Luke Schoonmaker (Cowboys)

All in all, the Browns have a good duo of outside corners in Tyson Campbell and Denzel Ward. The latter is the top-graded corner by PFF this season and Campbell has been a solid second corner on the other side.

The concern is that both Campbell and Ward have injury histories that warrant consideration. The latter has never played a full season, and the former has already missed time this season with a lower body injury in Week 2.

Bringing in competition for Myles Harden in the slot wouldn't be a bad idea. He has allowed more yards than any other player in the secondary this season.

Bringing in another defensive back would help ensure that the Browns have a defense that can keep them in games throughout the season. They would have more depth in the event that Ward or Campbell gets injured, while potentially upgrading the slot.

Potential Trade Targets: Amik Robertson (Commanders), Jarvis Brownlee (Jets), Paulson Adebo (Giants)

The Browns' Week 8 loss to the Steelers was an eye-opening reminder that the quarterback of the future is likely not on the roster right now.

Deshaun Watson has put together a season of impressive fourth-quarter heroics. Unfortunately, there was no fourth-quarter comeback to be had in Pittsburgh.

Watson topped 300 passing yards for the second consecutive week, but much of that production amounted to empty calories. The Browns' offense struggled to get going while the game was still competitive. Watson ran into multiple sacks throughout the afternoon and did little to bolster the rushing attack.

A midseason trade is the least likely route that the Browns will utilize to fix the problem. However, Ben Solak of ESPN threw out the idea that Cleveland should try to trade for Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert.

The idea is obviously a long shot. The Chargers are 0-7, but dealing a quarterback of Herbert's caliber in the middle of the season is still a risky move.

However, the Browns can't be discounted from making that kind of move. Watson is in the final year of his contract, and a smooth transition to a competent quarterback would be huge.

Potential Trade Target: Justin Herbert (Chargers)

articles.title: 2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 9
articles.summary: For NFL teams hoping to add a marquee player or move off of veteran contracts, the clock is ticking. The 2026 trade deadline will arrive at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday.
articles.body:
For NFL teams hoping to add a marquee player or move off of veteran contracts, the clock is ticking. The 2026 trade deadline will arrive at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday.

Once the deadline passes, trades will be off the board until the offseason.

Teams have certainly not waited until the last minute to make moves this season. We've already seen notable players like Marvin Harrison Jr., Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, and Jeffery Simmons change teams via the trade market. However, we could see a flood of activity over the final week.

As one unnamed source told NFL insider Jordan Schultz , "Get your popcorn ready."

Here, you'll find our updated and final list of top trade candidates, ranked according to factors like recent production, player upside, positional value, contract and cap implications, projected availability, and relevant recent trade buzz.

Since this is our final board before the deadline, we're expanding the list to our top 20 players, though we'll still provide trade values and potential suitors for those in the top 10.

Those projected trade values are based on factors such as position, player upside, player age, and any comparable deals.

20. Christian Barmore, DT, New England Patriots

New England Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore has a hefty four-year, $84 million contract that will take him off the board for some teams. However, he's a talented interior defender who "could be had," according to Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer .

19. Donte Jackson, CB, Los Angeles Chargers

The Los Angeles Chargers remain winless and could consider parting with cornerback Donte Jackson if he recovers from his lingering hamstring injury before next Tuesday. Jackson has appeared in only four games this season but appeared in all 17 last year while allowing an opposing passer rating of just 48.6 in coverage.

18. Rashod Bateman, WR, Baltimore Ravens

Baltimore Ravens receiver Rashod Bateman continues to slide out of the offensive game plan and has just 19 catches this season. With Lamar Jackson on injured reserve and Baltimore's season in jeopardy, the Ravens could decide it's time to trade Bateman.

17. Jermaine Johnson II, Edge, Tennessee Titans

Having already dealt Simmons, the one-win Tennessee Titans could consider parting with other players before Tuesday. Pass-rusher Jermaine Johnson II has three sacks this season and a ton of upside as a 2022 first-round pick. He's also set to be a free agent in the spring.

The Miami Dolphins are looking to build for the future with the NFL's youngest roster. While Jordyn Brooks is signed through 2029, he's also 29 and might not be a long-term fixture in Miami. He has 63 tackles already this season and would be a great addition to a contender in need of linebacker help.

Edge-rusher Josh Uche is another defender the Dolphins could consider moving if they become deadline sellers. The 28-year-old has 29 tackles and two sacks this season but is also playing on a one-year contract.

Safety Amani Hooker has been highly productive for the Titans in 2026. He leads the NFL with five interceptions and 114 interception-return yards. He's also allowed an opposing passer rating of just 60.2 in coverage. However, he also looms as a potential 2027 cap casualty.

Tennessee could cut him with a post-June 1 designation in the spring and save $10.3 million in cap space.

13. Jacoby Brissett, QB, Arizona Cardinals

The Arizona Cardinals recently moved former starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett to the QB3 role. With rookie Carson Beck set to back up Gardner Minshew, Brissett would be expendable. He'd be a top option for any team that needs a spot starter at quarterback.

Longtime Cardinals safety Budda Baker has made it clear that he'd prefer to stay in Arizona. Yet, the eight-time Pro Bowler would be a premier target for teams in need of secondary help. The 30-year-old continues to be a do-it-all defender and has already logged 51 tackles, 3.5 sacks, and an interception this season.

Running back Tony Pollard has racked up 665 scrimmage yards and five touchdowns while serving as Tennessee's best offensive player. According to ProFootballTalk's Mike Florio , "multiple teams" are interested in adding Pollard before Tuesday.

10. Tuli Tuipulotu, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 3rd-Round Pick

Los Angeles Chargers standout Tuli Tuipulotu would be a massive addition for any team in need of pass-rush help. He logged 13 sacks last season, has three sacks so far this year, and just turned 24 in September.

The USC product is also a fairly logical trade chip for the winless Chargers, as he is in the final year of his rookie deal and isn't guaranteed to stick around beyond this season. The issue is that, despite a 0-7 record, Los Angeles has been hesitant to sell.

On Monday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported on The Aftermath (beginning at the 1:05 mark) that the Chargers have shown "no inclination" to trade Tuipulotu (h/t Jeremy Fowler of ESPN).

This doesn't mean Tuipulotu shouldn't draw interest from other teams. It simply means there's virtually no chance he can be had for anything close to a bargain offer.

Potential Suitors: Buffalo Bills, Cleveland Browns

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 5th-Round Pick

The Philadelphia Eagles aren't necessarily in fire-sale mode, but general manager Howie Roseman potentially cracked the floodgates when he dealt center Cam Jurgens. Other teams are likely to come calling about some of Philly's better veterans.

Rapoport reported on Monday's episode of Good Morning Football (beginning around the 40-second mark) that, while Philly won't part with Saquon Barkley, players like cornerback Riq Woolen and guard Landon Dickerson are "the kinds of guys that the Eagles might look to sell."

Woolen played a notable role during the Seattle Seahawks' Super Bowl run last season, and he's been a valuable contributor for the Eagles in 2026. The 27-year-old hasn't been particularly efficient in coverage ( 112.8 passer rating allowed), but he has started all eight games for Philadelphia.

Having been a more effective cover man and a legitimate ball hawk early in his career, Woolen should be worth a flier to teams in need of secondary help.

Potential Suitors: Buffalo Bills, Pittsburgh Steelers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick

The Arizona Cardinals won their third game of the season on Sunday, thanks in large part to the efforts of quarterback Gardner Minshew. The Cardinals' former backup replaced Jacoby Brissett during the game and was recently installed as the new starter.

Assuming the Cardinals believe they can keep winning with Minshew, they probably won't be particularly interested in moving standout pass-rusher Josh Sweat. The 29-year-old has recorded three sacks, four tackles for loss, and nine quarterback pressures this season.

However, trading Sweat would save $10.9 million in cap space while potentially bringing the Cardinals a strong return.

"There is interest in Cardinals OLB Josh Sweat, per sources," ESPN's Adam Schefter posted on X on Sunday.

A strong offer could convince Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort to make a move.

Potential Suitors: Dallas Cowboys, Green Bay Packers

7. Jadeveon Clowney, Edge, Houston Texans

Projected Trade Value: 2027 5th-Round Pick

The Houston Texans have fallen well short of expectations this season and currently sit at 2-5. While they probably won't be interested in moving any centerpiece players, they might be willing to part with a player like Jadeveon Clowney, who signed a one-year, $5.5 million deal this offseason.

Moving Clowney would save Houston less than $1 million in cap space, but it could bring a reasonable return for a player who may not be with the team beyond this season.

According to Schefter , Clowney has drawn interest ahead of the trade deadline.

While Clowney will turn 34 in February, he remains an effective rotational defender. He has logged 1.5 sacks and two tackles for loss with the Texans this season, and he recorded 8.5 sacks and 12 tackles for loss with the Dallas Cowboys last year.

Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, Dallas Cowboys

6. Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

Projected Trade Value: 2027 2nd- and 5th-Round Picks

Mixed views continue to infiltrate the rumor mill regarding Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. The Jaguars have publicly stated that they plan to keep Thomas as part of their offensive game plan. However, not everyone around the league believes them.

"The Jacksonville Jaguars remain firm with teams that they won't deal WR Brian Thomas Jr.," The Athletic's Jonathan Jones wrote on Saturday. "'Yes they would,' one rival executive who doesn't need a wideout says."

While Thomas caught just one of two targets on Sunday, he did catch his second touchdown pass of the season. He has value to Jacksonville, even if he isn't poised to be the same playmaking Pro Bowler he was as a rookie in 2024.

Teams will and should continue to make offers for Thomas, given his status as an ancillary target for the Jags. However, it's clear that prying him away from Jacksonville will be costly.

Potential Suitors: New England Patriots, Pittsburgh Steelers

After trading Nelson and Buckner and then getting blown out for their sixth loss of the season on Sunday, the Indianapolis Colts may be on the verge of a fire sale.

Even if they're not, Josh Downs may be readily available for teams that need a receiver.

The 25-year-old pass-catcher officially requested a trade last week, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Considering he no longer wants to be in Indy, trading Downs would make sense for the Colts. He's in the final year of his rookie contract, and the odds of re-signing him in the offseason are probably slim.

Downs should also interest teams that lack receiver depth. He has three 500-yard seasons on his resume and has caught 30 passes for 330 yards and a touchdown so far this season.

Potential Suitors: Pittsburgh Steelers, San Francisco 49ers

Projected Trade Value: 2027 3rd-Round Pick

Rapoport didn't specifically mention Moro Ojomo alongside Woolen and Dickerson as potential trade chips for the Eagles. However, the talented defensive tackle would be a very sensible option if the Eagles are looking to part out their roster.

The 25-year-old has appeared in all eight games this season with three starts and has compiled 21 total tackles and three tackles for loss. Ojomo also has 10 quarterback pressures this season after logging 21 pressures and six sacks in 2025.

Ojomo is also in a contract year. While he's exactly the sort of young interior defender that most teams would jump at the chance to extend, Philadelphia isn't most teams.

The Eagles have already invested heavily in defensive tackles Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis. Giving a third defensive tackle a top-of-the-market contract would be incredibly difficult.

Teams eyeing Ojomo as a 2027 free-agent target should consider moving to acquire him now.

Potential Suitors: Carolina Panthers, Jacksonville Jaguars

3. Landon Dickerson, G, Philadelphia Eagles

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 2nd-Round Pick

The Seahawks didn't exactly see the instant impact they had hoped to get from Quenton Nelson. However, that shouldn't discourage teams from making a strong run at Landon Dickerson if he can be had.

Great guards are a rare commodity in the NFL, and Dickerson has been one, when healthy, throughout his career. He has spent much of the year on injured reserve with a knee injury, but he has been back for two full games now.

He has played 100 percent of the offensive snaps in all three of his 2026 appearances.

A three-time Pro Bowler who is still only 28 years old, Dickerson would be a great addition for teams looking to solidify their interior for the long term. He's under contract through 2028 and carries a base salary of just $1.2 million .

Potential Suitors: Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers

2. Khalil Mack, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

Despite their reluctance to move off of veterans at the deadline, the Chargers should listen to reasonable offers for future Hall of Famer Khalil Mack.

The nine-time Pro Bowler will turn 36 in February, and if he chooses to play next season, he'll likely opt to sign with a contender.

Based on what we've seen from L.A. this year, the Chargers probably won't be in the Super Bowl mix in 2027.

The Chargers can't expect to get much if Mack departs in free agency, either. Under the latest collective bargaining agreement , L.A. can receive no higher than a fifth-round compensatory pick because Mack has at least 10 accrued seasons.

Los Angeles could probably get more from a contender now. Mack has logged three sacks, five tackles for loss, and 11 QB pressures so far this season.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, San Francisco 49ers

1. Jonathan Taylor, RB, Indianapolis Colts

Running back Jonathan Taylor has rocketed to the top spot on our list after Rapoport reported on Good Morning Football that the Colts are "open" to trading the talented running back (beginning around the 1:00 mark).

Indianapolis obviously won't let Taylor go for cheap. He just signed a contract extension that runs through 2028, and trading him would cost the Colts $7.6 million in dead money. It would also leave Indy without its biggest star as it heads toward what will likely be a full-on rebuild in 2027.

The Colts already fired GM Chris Ballard, and it's hard to imagine that Shane Steichen will last beyond the season.

Still, Taylor is almost unquestionably the top running back likely to be available. He's a high-volume runner and receiver who currently ranks seventh in the NFL with 812 scrimmage yards and tied for seventh with eight touchdowns.

Taylor is the sort of offensive difference-maker who could help turn a playoff contender into a top-tier Super Bowl threat.

Potential Suitors: Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants

Contract information from OverTheCap . Advanced statistics from Pro Football Reference .

articles.title: Latest NFL Odds and Picks Factoring in New Weather Forecasts for Week 9 Schedule
articles.summary: The NFL season is approaching the halfway point, and the calendar has turned to November. While games haven't been inundated with wintry conditions just yet, the weather has started to turn.
articles.body:
The NFL season is approaching the halfway point, and the calendar has turned to November. While games haven't been inundated with wintry conditions just yet, the weather has started to turn.

This past Sunday, for example, we saw rain and mud impact a game that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers won without completing a pass.

Even when the weather has been fair, though, games have been very unpredictable this season. That trend is unlikely to change in Week 9, which will open with the Baltimore Ravens and Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night.

Here, we'll take an early look at the Week 9 slate, the latest odds, and the most accurate forecast information from The Weather Channel to make a few predictions.

Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) at Baltimore Ravens

Cincinnati Bengals (-3) vs. Atlanta Falcons (In Madrid, Retractable Roof)

Denver Broncos (-3) at Carolina Panthers

Dallas Cowboys (-5.5) at Indianapolis Colts (Retractable Roof)

New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs

Cleveland Browns (+2.5) at New Orleans Saints (Dome)

New York Giants (-3) at Philadelphia Eagles

Los Angeles Rams (-5.5) at Washington Commanders

Forecast: Mostly Sunny, Winds up to 10MPH, High of 60°F

Houston Texans (-4.5) at Los Angeles Chargers (Dome)

Las Vegas Raiders (+9.5) at San Francisco 49ers

Green Bay Packers (+2.5) at New England Patriots

Forecast: Partly Cloudy, Winds up to 10MPH, High of 57°F

Arizona Cardinals (+10.5) at Seattle Seahawks

Forecast: Showers Possible, Winds up to 15MPH, High of 60°F

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Chicago Bears

Forecast: Fair, Winds up to 10MPH, Low of 40°F

Buffalo Bills (-3) at Minnesota Vikings (Dome)

Byes: Pittsburgh Steelers, Tennessee Titans

Thursday's opener will be an interesting one. The Jaguars have played like legitimate Super Bowl contenders this season, while the Ravens have struggled to find consistency. To make matters worse, Baltimore recently placed Lamar Jackson on injured reserve with a thumb injury.

Backup Tyler Huntley is also injured, and third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano is dealing with an ankle injury.

"Expect him to have a chance to play on Thursday," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said of Fagnano, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley .

Starting a third-string rookie quarterback against an aggressive defense is less than ideal. However, Jacksonville is still on the road on a short week.

Action will resume on Sunday morning with the Cincinnati Bengals and Falcons in Santiago Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain.

Cincinnati has found another gear offensively over the last few weeks. While its defense remains a work in progress, the Falcons have been inconsistent offensively and may not be able to capitalize.

An exciting list of Sunday afternoon games includes an NFC West showdown between the Seattle Seahawks and Arizona Cardinals. Seattle has a top-tier defense and has been tough to beat at home. However, Arizona may have found something in new starting quarterback Gardner Minshew. The line is awfully large for a divisional battle.

Fans will also get to see a surging Green Bay Packers team against the New England Patriots. New England's defense should keep the Patriots in it at home, but a dwindling supply of healthy receivers could hurt the Pats.

Sunday night's battle between the Buccaneers and Chicago Bears is particularly intriguing. Chicago's offense is one of the best in the league, and its defensive front looked championship-caliber on Monday night with new standout Jeffery Simmons in the lineup.

The Bucs, though, have looked good while leaning on their defense and ground game. The X-factor here is the health of Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield, who only attempted three passes in Sunday's win over Atlanta.

The week will end with a pivotal matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings. Minnesota has arguably the top defense in the NFL, but the Bills have Josh Allen and an explosive offensive attack.

Can Kevin O'Connell coax a good performance from quarterback Kyler Murray against a vulnerable Bills defense? He'll have to if Minnesota hopes to upset Buffalo, even if it's a low-scoring game.

articles.title: Updated Buffalo Bills Team Needs One Week Ahead of the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: Only one game separates the Buffalo Bills from the 2026 NFL trade deadline, which takes place less than 24 hours after they play the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night.
articles.body:
Only one game separates the Buffalo Bills from the 2026 NFL trade deadline, which takes place less than 24 hours after they play the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night.

While the landscape could shift after Monday's game, it's officially crunch time to make a deal that puts this contender over the top.

With that in mind, here's an updated look at the five primary positions of potential weakness on this roster entering Week 9.

On the Roster: Dion Dawkins, Spencer Brown, Tylan Grable, Jude Bowry

Dawkins and Brown are a combined 60 years of age, and Brown's lingering back issues could become a problem. He missed Week 8 despite the Bills coming off the bye. Grable has performed well within a small sample in Brown's stead, but he's a 27-year-old with three career starts under his belt. And they'd obviously prefer not to have to use the rookie Bowry anytime soon.

This wasn't on the radar until Brown's back injury became a glaring issue. It escalated when the 28-year-old veteran said he "took enough drugs to sedate a small elephant" to play before the bye, yet still couldn't go against the Ravens.

Here's the rub. Miami's Austin Jackson would be an intriguing fit, but acquiring a competent tackle from a division rival is a massive reach. The reality at this position is that you're often SOL if you lose key guys, because nobody is trading away capable tackles in November. They really, really, really need Brown. And if not, they'll have to pray that Grable can seize the opportunity.

On the Roster: DJ Moore, Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir, Joshua Palmer, Skyler Bell, Greg Dortch

Moore has been superb when healthy but has been on the field for just 39 percent of the team's offensive snaps this season. Coleman and Shakir are tremendous secondary options, but Moore's injury issues combined with a hamstring injury suffered by Palmer in Week 8 are enough to raise concerns.

Moore limped off the field with a new injury Sunday against Baltimore, and there's a chance Palmer will miss time. That said, it helps that they could get Tyrell Shavers back from a torn ACL soon. They might view his return as their deadline addition at the position, considering his success as a mild breakout player in 2025.

Potential Trade Targets: Keenan Allen, Jauan Jennings, Kayshon Boutte

Allen is a six-time Pro Bowler who has been quite productive in Indianapolis and could make sense as a rental. Jennings experienced success in San Francisco but has not been used much by the Vikings. Boutte had some shiny moments with the Patriots last season before being dealt to the Texans, but with Marvin Harrison Jr. on board and Tank Dell rejoining the fray in Houston, he could be up for grabs at a cheap rate.

On the Roster: Christian Benford, Davison Igbinosun, Dee Alford, Maxwell Hairston, Te'Cory Couch

Benford struggled mightily early on as the No. 1 guy, and he has not received consistent support from the rest of the group. Igbinosun is an evolving rookie who has experienced a mix of highs and lows. Alford has been limited by injury, and Hairston has lost his starting role. The defense ranks 24th in the NFL in EPA allowed per pass play.

Benford has found his game, allowing just three total completions in Buffalo's last two games. Igbinosun is also getting better each week. Alford is a veteran with a track record, while Couch has suddenly emerged as a viable alternative in the slot.

Hairston might be the most talented deep-reserve cornerback in the league—though he could struggle to hold onto his active-roster spot if the Bills sign the recently re-signed Tre'Davious White from the practice squad to the 53-man roster.

Potential Trade Targets: Riq Woolen, Donte Jackson, Rasul Douglas

The 27-year-old Woolen has a Pro Bowl ceiling and could be part of a blowup in Philadelphia. Jackson could be in a similar situation with the Chargers, giving the Bills a shot at one of the most experienced and skilled cover guys in the league. A former Bills deadline acquisition, Douglas is a proven playmaker with plenty of experience. The Commanders don't appear to be contenders and could punt on his cheap, one-year deal.

On the Roster: Terrel Bernard, Dorian Williams, Kaleb Elarms-Orr, Joe Andreessen

Bernard's extensive injury history is a constant threat, and trusting Williams does not look like a winning strategy. Both starters have struggled more often than they've thrived this season. They're often out of position, sometimes due to poor angles or communication lapses. They're frequently pushed around, struggle in coverage and miss tackles in space.

Williams is coming off consecutive strong performances, and Bernard brought a new level of energy to the table in Week 8. It's possible Jim Leonhard has finally tapped into these guys following the bye week. Rookie fourth-round pick Kaleb Elarms-Orr is also making steady progress, and the whole unit remains healthy.

Potential Trade Targets: Zack Baun, Cody Barton, Mack Wilson

As a two-time Pro Bowler, Baun is the potential home run. He'd provide a massive immediate upgrade if the Eagles were willing to part with him in a lost season for the team, but the price tag would be high. Barton and Wilson would bolster the off-ball unit as rotational contributors who fit what Leonhard does.

On the Roster: Cole Bishop, Damar Hamlin, Jalon Kilgore

Gardner-Johnson proved to be a liability both during plays and after the whistle, leading to his abrupt release this week. Bishop has picked up his game after a shaky start to the year, but a contending team would prefer not to rely heavily on Hamlin or the rookie Kilgore.

Considering Geno Stone came off the practice squad and lit it up out of nowhere on Sunday, the depth is OK. But this team desperately needs an experienced and reliable deep-third presence who doesn't constantly miss tackles or occasionally spit at opponents. I get the feeling the CJGJ release is an indication they have something in the works.

Potential Trade Targets: Cam Bynum, Amani Hooker, Budda Baker, Elijah Molden

Bynum has become one of the most versatile and reliable free safeties in the league, and the Colts could potentially include him in their fire sale. He and Hooker are both 28-year-old ballhawks on rotting rosters, and they're relatively affordable this year but will count heavily against the cap in 2027.

Baker is an eight-time Pro Bowler hanging onto his prime with an uncompetitive Cardinals team, while Molden would bring extreme versatility to the Buffalo secondary if the Chargers are willing to deal him amid a dumpster-fire season.

articles.title: B/R's Week 9 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: You know the only thing that's better in fantasy football than feeling great in Week 8? Feeling fine in Week 9.
articles.body:
You know the only thing that's better in fantasy football than feeling great in Week 8? Feeling fine in Week 9.

Some folks have been all smiles for some time now. They drafted well, have dodged injuries and are on a collision course with the playoffs.

For others, thoughts of a postseason run have taken a far more Mora-esque turn. Foundational picks have floundered, injuries have piled up, and the losses keep coming.

Whether they're struggling, cruising or somewhere in between, every fantasy manager wants a win—and a reason to feel fine in Week 9.

Bleacher Report is here to help—with position-by-position PPR rankings, player notes, start-or-sit recommendations and sleepers.

Before we get to the heart of the matter with this week's sortable, searchable PPR rankings, it's weekly notes time.

The Overall Player Rankings included here can be of assistance in making "flex" lineup decisions. However, they do not include quarterbacks. If your league includes a "superflex" spot and you have a viable QB2, he should go in that spot.

Friendly tip: Joe Fagnano carries too much risk to recommend as a superflex option this week.

There are two teams on a bye in Week 9: the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans. It's not a hammer blow for fantasy managers, but there is no Jaylen Warren or Tony Pollard at running back this week.

Finally, with the NFL's trade deadline approaching, many fantasy managers are also looking to make a deal to strengthen their rosters for the season's second half. That's all well and good.

But keep your trade offers realistic. Your opening offer can leave room for negotiation, but an extreme lowball offer can end the conversation before it begins.

Eight weeks in, the top three quarterbacks in fantasy points aren't especially surprising—Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills, Joe Burrow of the Cincinnati Bengals and Drake Maye of the New England Patriots were all drafted as top-five fantasy options more often than not.

Kirk Cousins of the Las Vegas Raiders is another matter altogether.

After throwing for 247 yards and three scores (while adding another touchdown on the ground), Cousins sits fourth at the position in points. The 38-year-old has topped 20 fantasy points in five of eight games.

Not bad for a guy who was just expected to keep Fernando Mendoza's seat warm for a few weeks.

A difficult season for Lamar Jackson of the Baltimore Ravens took another turn in last week's loss to the Buffalo Bills. Returning from a hamstring injury, the signal-caller played just one snap before suffering a thumb injury that will require surgery. A return later this season remains possible, but his availability is uncertain.

Jackson wasn't the only quarterback who got dinged up in Week 8. His backup, Tyler Huntley, also exited the game with a toe injury that is expected to sideline him for multiple weeks, while Kyler Murray's availability for Week 9 is in question after he tweaked his hamstring in Week 8 against the Detroit Lions.

Last year, Matthew Stafford of the Los Angeles Rams led the NFL in passing yards and touchdown throws on the way to a third-place fantasy finish under center.

Stafford is second in passing yards and sixth in passing touchdowns through eight weeks, but his fantasy value has taken a major hit—he's just 18th in fantasy points per game at the position.

Jared Goff, Detroit Lions (at Miami Dolphins)

Goff doesn't get the run he should as an elite NFL quarterback—he's second in the NFC in passing yards per game and passer rating. He should have another productive game this week against a Dolphins defense that has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points per game to quarterbacks in 2026.

Caleb Williams, Chicago Bears (vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers)

The Chicago offense has been absolutely rolling of late, but Williams hasn't been a big beneficiary statistically—he's ninth in fantasy points per game among quarterbacks. Now he squares off against a surprisingly stout Buccaneers defense giving up the third-fewest fantasy points per game to quarterbacks.

Malik Willis, Miami Dolphins (vs. Detroit Lions)

Willis got off to a slow start, but he has picked up his play of late—since Miami's bye week Willis is quietly seventh in fantasy points among quarterbacks. Now he squares off against Detroit's high-octane offense and leaky defense—the Lions are allowing almost 25 fantasy points per game to the quarterback position.

There's little question who the "Big 3" running backs are this season. Jahmyr Gibbs of the Detroit Lions, Bijan Robinson of the Atlanta Falcons and Kenneth Walker III of the Kansas City Chiefs have been on quite the first-half rampage this season.

But D'Andre Swift of the Chicago Bears is on a nice little rip of his own in 2026.

The 27-year-old isn't lighting the world on fire on a per-carry basis. He's averaging 3.8 yards per tote and hasn't had 85 yards on the ground since the season opener.

But last week's win over the Seahawks was the second time this year Swift has scored three times on the ground, and no player has more touchdowns so far this season.

This week's matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the NFC's best run defense is a tough one, but Swift is almost impossible to sit at this point.

You had to know the injury bug wouldn't leave the running backs alone. Rookie Jeremiyah Love aggravated his ankle injury and is headed for a stint on injured reserve; and with Bam Knight in the NFL's concussion protocol, Tyler Allgeier appears slated for another heavy workload in Week 9 after gouging the Dallas Cowboys for almost 200 total yards.

Ashton Jeanty of the Las Vegas Raiders isn't injured, but his role diminished sharply last week. After struggling to produce on the ground for much of the season, he was replaced as the Raiders' lead back by rookie Mike Washington Jr.

Jeanty retained passing-down work, but Washington logged 25 carries to the 2025 first-rounder's two.

With the trade deadline rapidly approaching, there have been a lot of rumblings that Jonathan Taylor could be traded, with multiple teams mentioned as potential suitors .

It makes trusting Taylor in Week 9 a big ask unless the deal gets done soon—the Colts aren't going to risk him getting hurt if a trade appears imminent. That's a shame because he would be facing the NFL's worst run defense in Week 9.

Jonah Coleman, Denver Broncos (at Carolina Panthers)

Coleman shined for Denver in last week's big win over the Kansas City Chiefs, turning 15 touches into 104 total yards and a touchdown. Now Coleman takes on a Carolina team that has struggled against the run all season long—the Panthers have given up the second-most PPR points per game to running backs.

Derrick Henry, Baltimore Ravens (vs. Jacksonville Jaguars)

In the blink of an eye, the 2026 season has become a nightmare scenario for Henry. He has been held under 60 rushing yards in three straight contests. He has one score on the ground over the last month. With the Ravens down to their third-string quarterback, Henry is likely to face stacked fronts while Jackson and Huntley are sidelined.

Seth McGowan, Indianapolis Colts (vs. Dallas Cowboys)

This is admittedly a speculative call—if Taylor isn't traded before Sunday, McGowan's Week 9 workload becomes a major question mark. But McGowan has shown some flashes as a rookie, averaging a respectable 4.4 yards per carry. And Dallas is the only NFL team allowing over 150 yards per game on the ground.

Projections for Fantasy Pickups, Sleepers

There's still a lot of season left. But at the rate things are going, Jaxon Smith-Njigba of the Seattle Seahawks is going to have the most dominant season we have seen from a wide receiver since Cooper Kupp won receiving's "triple crown" in 2021.

After hauling in six passes for 118 yards and a touchdown Monday night against the Chicago Bears, Smith-Njigba has 64 catches for 985 yards and nine touchdowns. The catches are two off the pace for the league lead, but he is on pace to become the first 2,000-yard wide receiver in NFL history.

It's not like opponents don't know what the Seahawks are going to do offensively. There just isn't anything they can do to stop it.

Smith-Njigba is outscoring the No. 2 wideout (CeeDee Lamb of the Dallas Cowboys) by over six PPR points per game, and at his current pace he'll clear the runner-up by a larger margin than Kupp in 2021 or Ja'Marr Chase of the Cincinnati Bengals in 2024.

We managed to make it through a week without a big name at wide receiver going down with an injury, but we didn't get through the week completely unscathed—Kendrick Bourne of the Arizona Cardinals suffered an ankle injury that could end his season, and Joshua Palmer of the Buffalo Bills left Sunday's win over the Ravens with a hamstring issue.

Of course, just because no big-name receivers got hurt doesn't mean their fantasy value escaped the chipper-shredder. Entering Week 8, Zay Flowers of the Ravens was sixth in PPR points at the position. But with both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley out, Flowers was held catchless against the Bills on three targets.

There is no shortage of potent one-two punches at wideout in the NFL nowadays, and several of those dynamic duos are cooking over the season's first half.

Christian Watson and Matthew Golden of the Green Bay Packers both rank inside the top 10 in PPR points. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens of the Cowboys are both inside the top 15. And Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins of the Cincinnati Bengals both sit inside the top 20.

WR Demario Douglas, New England Patriots (vs. Green Bay Packers)

Douglas rebounded from a quiet first half last week to finish the win over the Miami Dolphins with three catches for 76 yards and a touchdown. He could be New England's de facto No. 1 receiver again in Week 9 against a Packers defense giving up the ninth-most PPR points per game to wide receivers in 2026.

D.J. Moore, Buffalo Bills (at Minnesota Vikings)

Moore made his return to the Bills lineup last week and had a good game—four catches on seven targets for 82 yards and a touchdown. But Moore got dinged up (again) against the Ravens, and now he takes on the NFL's best pass defense in a Vikings team allowing less than 155 yards a game through the air.

Caleb Douglas, Miami Dolphins (vs. Detroit Lions)

Douglas has been heating up of late—he has six receptions for 113 yards and a pair of touchdowns over the last two weeks. The Dolphins are going to have to throw the ball to keep up with Detroit's offense in Week 9, and the Lions have the worst pass defense in the NFL.

In a season that has featured no shortage of surprises, there haven't been that many at the tight end position.

It's hardly a surprise that Trey McBride of the Arizona Cardinals leads all fantasy tight ends in PPR points: He's third in the NFL in targets and leads the league with 66 receptions. It's also no upset that Brock Bowers of the Las Vegas Raiders is hot on his heels, as he is the only tight end averaging 20-plus PPR points per game.

Isaiah Likely of the New York Giants was a trendy breakout candidate this year, and so far he has been as advertised. George Kittle of the San Francisco 49ers is, well, George Kittle. Harold Fannin Jr. of the Cleveland Browns. Tucker Kraft of the Green Bay Packers. Sam LaPorta of the Detroit Lions.

For the most part, the established names have delivered.

Week 8 was relatively light on tight end injuries. However, there were a couple of TEs who went down. Jake Ferguson of the Dallas Cowboys left Sunday's loss to Arizona with a sprained ankle, while Hunter Henry of the New England Patriots hurt his foot.

The top of the tight end leaderboard may feature a lot of big names, but one is conspicuously absent. Last season, only McBride had more PPR points than Kyle Pitts Sr. of the Atlanta Falcons. But after two catches for six yards in last week's loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Pitts is barely inside the top-20 in PPR points for the season.

It's that much worse for Mark Andrews of the Baltimore Ravens. The one-time fantasy star was already teetering on the brink of fantasy irrelevance—he sits 24th in PPR points after eight weeks. Now, with the Ravens passing game in tatters, Andrews barely rates a roster spot in most leagues.

Sam LaPorta, Detroit Lions (at Miami Dolphins)

LaPorta isn't especially happy that his contract hasn't been extended, but it hasn't affected his production—he's seventh in PPR points among tight ends. His two outings since Detroit's bye week have been pretty sleepy, but he'll wake up Sunday in a favorable matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Dalton Kincaid, Buffalo Bills (at Minnesota Vikings)

Kincaid has been mostly solid for fantasy managers this season—he has four games with double-digit PPR points and ranks inside the top-10 tight ends for the season. Getting a fifth on Monday night will be tricky—the Vikings are giving up just over seven PPR points a game to the position.

Tyler Higbee, Los Angeles Rams (at Washington Commanders)

After a mini hot streak, Higbee has cooled way down—the veteran has just 10 PPR points in his last three games combined. This week's trip to the nation's capital should help warm things up—the Commanders have surrendered the second-most PPR points per game to tight ends in 2026.

For most of this season, the Minnesota Vikings have been at the top of the fantasy defense totem pole. But after eight weeks, there's a surprise new No. 1.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers aren't loaded with star power—Todd Bowles' team this year is relatively young on that side of the ball. But the Buccaneers have been stout against the run—only the Jaguars are giving up fewer yards per game on the ground.

The team leads the league with 16 takeaways after picking off Michael Penix Jr. four times last week. And while the pass rush hasn't been the league's best, it has been respectable.

This week's matchup with the red-hot Chicago Bears isn't a good one. Next week's trip to Detroit is worse.

But Tampa is a hard defense to drop right now.

The Houston defense has been a major disappointment for fantasy managers to this point in the season—a team that was among the first defenses drafted ranks outside the top 20 in points.

This week, the Texans take on the winless Chargers coming out of the bye. It's last-chance time for the Texans—and then some.

The Texans aren't the only big-name defense that hasn't met expectations—a Los Angeles Rams squad that was supposed to be an unstoppable juggernaut has dealt with injuries and poor play in equal measure on the way to a 4-4 record. What was supposed to be an every-week must-start is now a "meh" matchup play.

And then there were four. That's how many kickers have attempted double-digit field goals this year without a miss—Cincinnati's Evan McPherson, Tyler Bass of the Bills, Ryan Fitzgerald of the Panthers and Tampa's Chase McLaughlin.

McLaughlin now leads the position in points despite entering the season with little fantasy fanfare.

Cincinnati Bengals Defense (at Atlanta Falcons)

The Bengals have turned a penchant for big plays into the fifth-most fantasy points per game among defenses, and the Falcons have allowed the most fantasy points per game in the NFC to the position.

Andre Szmyt, Cleveland Browns (at New Orleans Saints)

Szmyt has made something of a habit out of hitting game-winners this season, and his 16 made field goals on the year ranks inside the top-10 at the position. He'll have his chances Sunday in the Big Easy.

The Vikings have been too consistently productive to drop, and for managers in shallower leagues rostering a second defense can be problematic. But the Bills are a lousy fantasy matchup, giving up the fifth-fewest fantasy points per game to defenses.

Chase McLaughlin, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (at Chicago Bears)

McLaughlin has topped 10 fantasy points in each of the last three weeks, and no kicker in the NFC is averaging more points per game. But the Bears are the second-worst fantasy matchup in the league for kickers—something has to give.

New Orleans Saints Defense (vs. Cleveland Browns)

The Saints have not been a good defensive team this year—they rank in the bottom-five in both yards and points allowed. But they have made enough big plays to be a middling fantasy squad, and the Browns are surrendering over four sacks per contest this season.

Drew Stevens, Washington Commanders (vs. Los Angeles Rams)

Stevens was productive last week, hitting on four of five field goals—including a 56-yarder. The Rams have been kind to the kicker position in 2026, allowing the fourth-most fantasy points per game.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes deemed fake and fraud as Chiefs suffer back-to-back losses against Seahawks and Broncos
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs' impressive start to the 2026 NFL season has taken an uncomfortable turn.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs' impressive start to the 2026 NFL season has taken an uncomfortable turn. After opening their campaign with five straight victories, Patrick Mahomes and his teammates have suddenly lost their grip, raising fresh questions about their ability to compete with the league's strongest sides. Two defeats have changed the conversation around Andy Reid's team, and FOX Sports host Rob Parker has delivered a particularly harsh verdict. His criticism goes beyond the results, putting the Chiefs' reputation and their early-season success under the spotlight.Rob Parker questions Patrick Mahomes and Chiefs after two straight defeatsKansas City entered the season with considerable expectations, especially after adding Kenneth Walker III to strengthen its rushing attack. The early results appeared to justify the optimism. Wins over Denver, Indianapolis, Miami, Las Vegas and the Los Angeles Chargers gave the Chiefs a perfect 5-0 record.However, their performances against Seattle and Denver have exposed problems that were less visible during that winning run.Parker believes the Chiefs received too much praise before proving themselves against tougher competition. Speaking on FOX's The Odd Couple with Rob Parker and Kelvin Washington, he questioned whether Kansas City deserved its early-season reputation.“I think the Kansas City Chiefs, and I know a lot of people wanted to jump on the bandwagon and say, ‘Oh, they’re back, and they’re great,’ and all of the other stuff that comes with it,” said Parker. “But I’m convinced after watching the last couple of weeks that they’re not the team that people thought they were. The Kansas City Chiefs are frauds. They’re fugazi. Is there another F I can find?“Andy Reid should be fired. No, that part I’ll take away. Fake. Frauds. Fugazi. That is what the Kansas City Chiefs are. And phonies with an F.”His comments followed a miserable 20-3 defeat against Seattle, where Mahomes failed to lead Kansas City into the red zone. The quarterback finished with 165 passing yards, no touchdowns and one interception. The Chiefs also managed only 213 total yards, highlighting the extent of their offensive struggles.Patrick Mahomes faces another setback after Broncos lossThe Chiefs had an opportunity to silence their critics against Denver, but another late collapse made matters worse.Kansas City held a 24-13 advantage early in the fourth quarter. However, Bo Nix and the Broncos mounted a comeback, eventually taking a 28-24 lead with less than two minutes remaining.The defeat carried historical significance for Mahomes. Before the game, he had an 80-2 record when the Chiefs held a lead of at least 10 points in the fourth quarter, including postseason games. That remarkable record is now 80-3.Parker pointed directly to these performances when explaining his frustration.“Two weeks ago, they scored three points and were never in the red zone. Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs were never in the red zone,” he added. “I thought they had the ultimate running back. Now, they’re good to go. All they had to do was add a running game, and now you can’t stop Patrick. Three points, never in the red zone against Seattle in a 20-3 loss.“Then the Broncos…they (Chiefs) blown 11 points. 80-and-2 in Patrick Mahomes era. They never gave it up. They gave it up like a $2 w***e on Sunday. That’s what they did. And now the two best teams they played, they’re 0-2. This was the Chiefs up a year ago when they didn’t make the playoffs.”Mahomes still had one final chance to rescue the Broncos game. Kansas City reached Denver's one-yard line with four seconds left, but a false-start penalty pushed the offense backwards. Malcolm Roach then sacked Mahomes on fourth-and-goal to seal the result.The Chiefs now face an important test of character. Their early winning streak showed what this team could achieve, but the latest defeats have exposed questions that only stronger performances can answer. For Mahomes and Reid, responding on the field is now more important than answering their critics.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Los Falcons ya conocen el frío madrileño: ocho horas de viaje, diez grados menos y entrenamiento a 'las cuatro de la mañana'
articles.standfirst: El equipo que jugará de local en el Santiago Bernabéu ya ha aterrizado en la ciudad y se ha ido directo a la ciudad deportiva del Real Madrid a entrenar
articles.summary: El equipo que jugará de local en el Santiago Bernabéu ya ha aterrizado en la ciudad y se ha ido directo a la ciudad deportiva del Real Madrid a entrenar
articles.body: Los Atlanta Falcons ya están en Madrid. Y no han tardado en ponerse en marcha. Nada más aterrizar en la capital de España, y después de un viaje de más de ocho horas, se han ido directos a la ciudad deportiva del Real Madrid, donde estarán preparando estos días el encuentro del domingo. Allí les ha recibido el característico frío mañanero de la capital. A su llegada el termómetro no superaba los 8ºC, diez menos de los que hacía en Atlanta, Georgia. Lejos de irse a descansar, se han ido directos al terreno de juego y han entrenado a las 10 de la mañana hora española (6 horas menos para ellos). "Normalmente un miércoles tenemos un entrenamiento normal, pero con el vuelo, lo que hemos hecho es un entreno de movilidad rápido para asegurarnos que se mueven después del avión. Luego estaremos un rato por aquí y más tarde al hotel. Vamos a centrarnos hoy más en el lado mental que en el físico", explicaba Kevin Stefanski, entrenador principal de los Atlanta Falcons en rueda de prensa. Tal y como ha confirmado el 'Head Coach' del equipo de Georgia, el entrenamiento se ha reducido a una serie de ejercicios de movilidad. En él hemos podido ver a las grandes estrellas del 'equipo de las águilas'. Tanto Bijan Robinson, como Drake London y Kyle Pitts han estado presentes en el césped de la ciudad deportiva del Real Madrid y estarán disponibles para el partido del domingo. Sobre el 7 de los Falcons, Stefanski se ha deshecho en elogios: "El señor ha bendecido a Bijan. Tiene una combinación de fuerza y agilidad. Parece que lo han fabricado en un laboratorio". B. Robinson y el resto de sus compañeros entrenarán el jueves y el viernes de forma más intensa y táctica. El entrenador de los Falcons también ha querido tener palabras de agradecimiento para la capital española: "Me encantaría que los fans de aquí entiendan el equipo que somos. Estamos encantados de tener el apoyo de la ciudad y jugar en casa. Estamos encantados de estar aquí. Daremos un paseo y conoceremos la ciudad, el viernes iremos a cenar e incluso viene la familia". Sobre el club y el estadio no ha querido mojarse en exceso: "No se mucho de fútbol. Tengo mucho respeto por el Real Madrid y lo que quiere decir el equipo para el mundo. Soy lo consciente de lo importante que es el Bernabéu. Quiero dar las gracias al Real Madrid, es una empresa increíble y tiene unas instalaciones espectaculares.

articles.title: Tyler Huntley Injury Update, Ravens QB to Undergo Season-Ending Surgery Amid Lamar's Absence
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens backup quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season due to a turf toe injury, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens backup quarterback Tyler "Snoop" Huntley is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season due to a turf toe injury, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added that the injury requires surgery, and is similar to the turf toe issue that caused Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow to miss 10 games last season.

In addition to Huntley being on the shelf, Ravens starting quarterback Lamar Jackson is out for at least the next month after being placed on injured reserve due to a thumb injury requiring surgery.

After missing three games with an ankle injury, Jackson returned to start against the Buffalo Bills this past weekend, but he hurt his thumb on Baltimore's first offensive play from scrimmage.

Jackson was removed from the game, did not return and was later seen with a brace on his throwing hand and thumb.

Huntley, who had started the previous three games, replaced Jackson, but he only lasted 10 plays himself before having to be removed in favor of emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano.

With Fagnano playing most of the game, the Ravens went on to suffer a one-sided, 36-10 loss.

Huntley, 28, has been a reliable backup for Baltimore for the past six seasons, starting 14 games for the Ravens during that time.

A Pro Bowl selection in 2022 when he went 2-2 as a starter and helped lead the Ravens to the playoffs in Jackson's absence, Huntley is 6-8 overall as the Ravens' starter, including a 1-2 mark this season.

Appearing in five games overall this season, Huntley was completing 69.1 percent of his passes for 727 yards, four touchdowns and one interception, while also rushing for 76 yards and a score.

With Huntley now out for the rest of the campaign and head coach Jesse Minter calling Jackson's injury "potentially" season-ending as well, the Ravens are now turning to Fagnano.

The undrafted rookie out of UConn has already been named the starter for Baltimore's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night.

Fagnano largely struggled in his first taste of NFL action against Buffalo, going 10-of-21 for 91 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, while getting sacked three times and fumbling once.

The Ravens could possibly make a deal for a quarterback ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, and Fagnano's performance in a tough game against the Jags may play a role in that decision.

As things stand, the Ravens are 4-4 and still very much in the playoff race in the AFC, so going out and getting a veteran quarterback who can potentially keep them in contention may be a major priority for the front office over the next week.

articles.title: Ravens QB Tyler Huntley reportedly suffered season-ending turf toe injury after replacing Lamar Jackson vs. Bills
articles.summary: Huntley came in for Jackson after Jackson injured his throwing thumb on the first offensive play of the game.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens are now down their top two quarterbacks for the foreseeable future.

According to ESPN , the turf toe injury that backup quarterback Tyler Huntley suffered against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday is season-ending. Ravens coach Jesse Minter had announced Tuesday that No. 3 QB Joe Fagnano would start Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Lamar Jackson was placed on injured reserve Tuesday after suffering an injury to his thumb on his throwing hand on the first offensive play of the game in the loss to the Bills. Jackson needs surgery on his right thumb.

Huntley immediately replaced Jackson, but he suffered his turf toe injury before halftime and didn't return to the game. Before his injury, Huntley attempted just four passes.

Huntley made three starts in 2026 as Jackson was sidelined with an ankle injury. The Bills game was Jackson's first start since he suffered that ankle injury on Oct. 4 against the Tennessee Titans.

Fagnano is an undrafted rookie from UConn who took his first NFL regular-season snaps after taking over for Huntley. He was 10 of 21 for 91 yards and an interception. He practiced Tuesday with a brace on his right ankle after injuring that during the game.

Behind Fagnano, the Ravens signed former practice squad quarterback Austin Reed and also added Kedon Slovis to the roster with Jackson and Huntley out.

Huntley, 28, has been Jackson's primary backup for his entire career outside of spending the 2024 season with the Miami Dolphins. Over six years with the Ravens, he's appeared in 30 games and made 14 starts, infamously making the 2022 Pro Bowl after appearing in six games that season.

Baltimore is now 4-4 after three straight losses and the absence of Jackson and Huntley could end up making their hopes of winning the AFC North disappear as every other team in the division is above .500. After playing Jacksonville this week, the Ravens host the Chargers on Monday Night Football.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Daniel Jones, Potential Ravens QB Trade Targets After Lamar, Huntley Injuries
articles.summary: Amid uncertainty about Lamar Jackson's status for the remainder of the 2026 season, the Baltimore Ravens are seeking help at quarterback prior to the trade deadline as they try to stay in the AFC playoff race.
articles.body:
Amid uncertainty about Lamar Jackson's status for the remainder of the 2026 season, the Baltimore Ravens are seeking help at quarterback prior to the trade deadline as they try to stay in the AFC playoff race.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , some of the options the Ravens are looking at include Daniel Jones and Tyson Bagent.

In the same report, Dan Graziano noted the Ravens will "work to solve the problem" with Jackson out for the time being and are "open to a number of ideas" at the quarterback spot with Jacoby Brissett cited as someone they could "look into" acquiring.

Jackson returned on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills after missing three games then injured his thumb on his first pass attempt.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters after the 36-10 loss to Buffalo that Jackson would undergo surgery and be placed on injured reserve.

Bagent immediately stood out as a potential trade option for Baltimore because Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle came from the Chicago Bears where the two worked together last season.

The Bears may not be eager to trade Bagent since Caleb Williams has already missed time this season, though they did get one quality start from Case Keenum during Williams' absence that might make head coach Ben Johnson comfortable if he had to step in.

Few teams are harder to figure out right now than the Colts, even though they have acknowledged their need to sell by trading away Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner.

The Colts are reportedly open to trading Jonathan Taylor, but they still played him 38 offensive snaps and risked a potential injury in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Jones' availability might be even harder to figure out because head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Monday he will remain the starting quarterback.

Of the potential quarterback options mentioned by Fowler and Graziano, Brissett might be the most available. He was benched by the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in favor of Gardner Minshew II, who led the offense to 23 points in the fourth quarter and overtime in a 33-30 victory over the Dallas Cowboys.

Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur announced Minshew will remain the starter going forward and rookie Carson Beck will be the No. 2, leaving Brissett as the emergency third quarterback.

If the Cardinals are demoting Brissett to the point he may not even be active on gamedays barring injuries to the top two quarterbacks, the Ravens could presumably throw a late-round draft pick at Arizona to make a deal.

There's no good situation for the Ravens right now because Tyler Huntley also suffered a turf toe injury that is expected to keep him out for the remainder of the season. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is set to make his first career start on Thursday night against the Jaguars.

It has not been determined if Jackson will miss the rest of the season, but an IR stint will keep him out for at least the next four weeks. The schedule does help them because they have a bye in Week 13, meaning Jackson could theoretically be back on Dec. 13 with five games remaining.

The Ravens have to be in a position where they are still contending to make it worth potentially playing Jackson if he is able to suit up, but they will need to add reinforcements regardless because the depth chart of Fagnano and Kedon Slovis is not likely to yield positive results.

articles.standfirst: La capital española se prepara para numerosos eventos y experiencias a lo largo de esta semana
articles.summary: La capital española se prepara para numerosos eventos y experiencias a lo largo de esta semana
articles.body: La NFL convertirá Madrid en el epicentro del fútbol americano durante la semana previa al enfrentamiento entre Atlanta Falcons y Cincinnati Bengals, que se disputará el domingo 8 de noviembre en el Santiago Bernabéu. La liga ha preparado tres grandes experiencias para acercar este deporte a los aficionados. La primera será la NFL House, que abrirá sus puertas los días 6 y 7 de noviembre en la Casa de las Alhajas, en la plaza de San Martín, de 12:00 a 20:00 horas. Los visitantes podrán contemplar el trofeo Vince Lombardi y los 60 anillos de campeón de la Super Bowl, además de disfrutar de videojuegos, actividades interactivas, exposiciones y experiencias creativas con inteligencia artificial. La entrada será gratuita con inscripción previa en NFL OnePass. También estará la NFL Experience, instalada en la plaza de España los mismos días, de 10:00 a 19:00 horas. Contará con un campo de flag football, pruebas de habilidad, música en directo, leyendas de la competición, cheerleaders y las mascotas de ambas franquicias. Por último, el Bernabéu acogerá la NFL Shop, tienda oficial abierta del 5 al 9 de noviembre, donde se podrán adquirir camisetas, productos exclusivos del partido y colecciones especiales diseñadas para la ocasión. Asimismo, a modo de previa del encuentro del domingo, este martes tuvo lugar un 'Media Summit' para medios de comunicación en el que participaron representantes de las empresas implicadas en la organización del encuentro. Uno de ellos fue César Cernuda, presidente de NetApp, compañía que ejercerá como 'partner' principal del partido. Cernuda destacó la importancia de esta alianza y el papel de la tecnología en un acontecimiento de estas características. "Es un privilegio decir que somos el partner principal. Somos la compañía líder en el mundo de almacenamiento y gestión de datos. Operamos en más de 100 países. Llevamos muchos años trabajando con la NFL. Cuando decidimos avanzar en la alianza con ellos es el plan de estrategia internacional. Dentro del estadio se genera mucho volumen de datos y nosotros lo que hacemos es que todo sea más accesible", explicó. También intervino Alex Wicks, CEO del estadio Santiago Bernabéu, que puso en valor la dimensión internacional del recinto y el impacto que supone recibir una competición como la NFL. "El Bernabéu no solo es el mejor estadio, sino el mejor recinto del mundo. La colaboración con la NFL es un ejemplo perfecto de cómo podemos atraer a nuevos públicos y darnos a conocer en un escenario mundial. Queremos asegurarnos de que el estadio siga teniendo un impacto positivo en la ciudad. El beneficio económico fue de unos 70 millones de euros. Queremos aportar más beneficio tanto este año como en los próximos. Las audiencias e interacciones no distan mucho de cuando el Madrid juega en un Clásico", señaló.
