articles.title: Commanders' Kinlaw, Payne, McNichols Placed on Injured Reserve After Win vs. Eagles
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders placed defensive tackles Javon Kinlaw, Daron Payne on injured reserve alongside running back Jeremy McNichols, the team announced on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders placed defensive tackles Javon Kinlaw, Daron Payne on injured reserve alongside running back Jeremy McNichols, the team announced on Tuesday.

According to Adam Schefter of ESPN, Kinlaw underwent season-ending surgery on his MCL.

Kinlaw missed Washington's victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night due to a knee injury he suffered against the San Francisco 49ers. Kinlaw tallied 13 tackles and one sack this season.

Payne has spent his entire nine-year career in Washington, but he is expected to become an unrestricted free agent after this season. The 29-year-old defensive tackle was named as a potential trade candidate prior to his injury, but any chance of a move came to an end when he suffered a season-ending Jones fracture during practice last Friday.

Kinlaw and Payne have both served as vital parts of the Commanders defensive line over the past two seasons. Washington will now look to alleviate their losses by turning to defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton, who was designated to return from injured reserve last week.

McNichols missed multiple games earlier this season due to a quadriceps injury and was just getting adjusted to Washington's backfield rotation, but he will likely miss the remainder of the season after suffering a foot injury on Sunday. The 31-year-old running back is expected to miss multiple months, according to Tashan Reed of the Washington Post .

The Commanders' season hasn't gone as they hoped, and they're heading into a matchup against the Los Angeles Rams with with a 2-4-1 record.

articles.title: New Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors on NFL Teams' Stance on Colts' Asking Price at 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Six days away from the NFL trade deadline, the Indianapolis Colts are in a good position to potentially get the value they want for Jonathan Taylor if they decided to move their star running back.
articles.body:
Six days away from the NFL trade deadline, the Indianapolis Colts are in a good position to potentially get the value they want for Jonathan Taylor if they decided to move their star running back.

Per ESPN's Dan Graziano and Jeremy Fowler , the Colts continue to have a high asking price for Taylor and "enough teams" are interested that they don't yet have to think about lowering their demands.

"The Colts are still asking for a lot for RB Jonathan Taylor and taking the stance that they don't need to move him," Graziano reported.

According to Fowler, the feeling among NFL executives is the Colts could be holding out for the "equivalent" value of a first-round pick.

Fowler added the execs believe Taylor is worth a second-round selection plus an additional pick, with one AFC executive quoted as saying the Colts "want a bunch" right now.

Graziano cited the New York Giants as a team he "wouldn't be a surprised" if they were the one that made the move for Taylor. The Minnesota Vikings are another team that has frequently been connected to running backs, including Taylor, leading up to the trade deadline.

Using the standard NFL draft trade value chart , the lowest value for a first-round pick at No. 32 is 590 points. The Giants' second- and third-round selections have a combined value of 610 points, which would slot between picks No. 30 and 31 in terms of value.

The closest parallel to Taylor is the Christian McCaffrey trade to the San Francisco 49ers in 2022. San Francisco gave the Carolina Panthers a second-, third- and fourth-round pick in 2023 and a fifth-rounder in 2024.

McCaffrey was in his age-26 season at the time, but had only played 10 games in the previous two years combined due to injuries. Taylor is in his age-27 season and hasn't missed a game since Week 7 of the 2024 campaign.

With the Colts embracing their need to rebuild, they are in a tricky spot with Taylor. Trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week made sense because both players were over the age of 30 and in the final season of their current contracts, making it less likely they would be brought back.

Taylor just signed a two-year extension in August that runs through the 2028 season, so in theory the Colts could rebuild their roster to be back in playoff contention sooner than later.

Complicating the situation, though, is the Colts don't control their first-round pick in the upcoming draft as a result of the Sauce Gardner trade. Based on the current standings , their pick would be No. 4 overall going to the New York Jets.

articles.title: Justin Herbert's Struggles Discussed by NFL Exec, 'Don't Know How it Gets Better,' for Chargers QB
articles.summary: There is reportedly some doubt within the NFL regarding whether Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert can turn around what has been a nightmarish season thus far.
articles.body:
There is reportedly some doubt within the NFL regarding whether Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert can turn around what has been a nightmarish season thus far.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler spoke this week to an anonymous AFC executive who said of Herbert, "He doesn't seem comfortable in the offense. I don't know that it's a great schematic fit for his talents. He's throwing a lot of picks where he simply isn't seeing defenders. I don't know how it gets better."

Regarding Herbert in offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's system, ESPN's Dan Graziano noted that he has heard "similar things" about him being an "awkward fit" due to the belief that adjusting at the line of scrimmage may not be his strong suit.

Coach: Herbert 'Incredibly Uncomfortable'

Hot Seat Check on Struggling NFL Coordinators 🌡️

However, an anonymous NFL defensive coach tried to give Herbert the benefit of the doubt, telling Fowler, "The entire team has been devastated around him. The O-line is a mess, the running game is bad, and the skill guys aren't very good. It's nearly impossible to have success with that setup."

No matter how you slice it, the Chargers are 0-7, making them the last winless team in the NFL this season.

They entered the campaign as a popular pick to vie for an AFC West title and potentially even contend for a Super Bowl berth out of the AFC.

The optimism was understandable, given that L.A. went 11-6 and reached the playoffs in each of Jim Harbaugh's first two seasons as head coach.

On top of that, the Chargers added an offensive guru in McDaniel, who guided some high-flying offenses during his time as head coach of the Miami Dolphins.

None of that has translated to success, though, and Herbert has seemingly regressed in a big way during his seventh NFL season.

The 28-year-old is completing 61.8 percent of his passes for 1,398 yards, five touchdowns and a league-high 10 interceptions, while also rushing for 183 yards.

There have been no obvious signs of improvement, but perhaps a softer upcoming schedule can help Herbert and the Bolts finally get back on track, as they are set to face a Baltimore Ravens team without star quarterback Lamar Jackson and the New York Jets in back-to-back games following this coming Sunday's home game against the Houston Texans.

articles.title: Cowboys' George Pickens Eyed by Teams in New NFL Trade Rumors After Historic Loss to Cardinals
articles.summary: Even though the Dallas Cowboys don't appear eager to become sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline despite a 3-5 record through Week 8, teams are at least hoping they will test the market for George Pickens.
articles.body:
Even though the Dallas Cowboys don't appear eager to become sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline despite a 3-5 record through Week 8, teams are at least hoping they will test the market for George Pickens.

Per ESPN's Dan Graziano , opposing clubs are "wondering" if Pickens might become available if the Cowboys lose again this weekend to the Indianapolis Colts.

Graziano did note his sense is the Cowboys won't consider dealing their star wide receiver before the Nov. 10 deadline.

This comes after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said on Tuesday's episode of The Pat McAfee Show he has been told a Pickens trade is "not happening."

The Cowboys fell to 3-5 this season after blowing a 14-point fourth quarter lead at home to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. They allowed 23 points between the fourth quarter and overtime to lose.

Per the Elias Sports Bureau (h/t ESPN's Todd Archer ), the Cowboys tied a franchise record by blowing a 14-point fourth-quarter lead to lose a game.

Dallas has not historically been a team that trades away players during the season. Jerry Jones has aggressively made deals to add talent in recent years, including Quinnen Williams last year and Joey Porter Jr. on Oct. 1.

The last in-season trade the Cowboys made in which they gave up a player without receiving a player back was in 2020 when they dealt Everson Griffen to the Detroit Lions for a conditional sixth-round pick.

Pickens would make sense to break that trend since he is playing on the franchise tag and it seemed like offseason talks with the Cowboys about a long-term deal never really happened based on how quickly executive vice president Stephen Jones said after they applied the tag there would be no multiyear extension.

A huge complicating factor is the Cowboys would have to consider themselves out of the playoff race, which doesn't seem to be the case because Stephen Jones said Monday they are still open to potentially adding to their roster.

If the Cowboys lose to a Colts team that has already entered sell-off mode by trading Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner and is coming off a 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8, perhaps Jerry and Stephen Jones change their deadline tune.

But until the Cowboys provide any evidence they don't view themselves as capable of getting back in the playoff race in the NFC, there's no reason to think Pickens will be moved within the next six days.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk Applies for NFL Reinstatement, Will Report to 49ers Facility, Agent Says
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk has taken another step in his attempt to return to the NFL by applying for reinstatement after being placed on the reserve/left squad list by the San Francisco 49ers in December 2025.
articles.body:
Brandon Aiyuk has taken another step in his attempt to return to the NFL by applying for reinstatement after being placed on the reserve/left squad list by the San Francisco 49ers in December 2025.

Drew Rosenhaus, who was hired as Aiyuk's agent on Monday, told ESPN's Adam Schefter the veteran wide receiver has turned in the required paperwork to apply for reinstatement and he will report to the 49ers' facilities on Friday.

ESPN's Nick Wagoner added this is the first step from Aiyuk's side to force the 49ers into trading or releasing him. The team's preference has been to find a trade, but Wagoner noted it would "seem unlikely" and a release would be the next logical step.

ESPN's Dan Graziano reported that he does not expect the Washington Commanders to be "in the market" for Aiyuk, noting that the wide receiver made remarks "that make it unlikely" a deal happens.

Aiyuk officially hired Rosenhaus to represent him on Monday. He revealed on social media in June that he had been without an agent since November 2025 after terminating his standard representation agreement with Ryan Williams of Athletes First.

The situation between Aiyuk and the 49ers has been going on for nearly one full calendar year. The club voided the remaining guaranteed money in his contract last November for reportedly going months without attending meetings and declining to participate in other team activities.

That later led to the Niners putting Aiyuk on the reserve/left squad list on Dec. 13. Head coach Kyle Shanahan and general manager John Lynch have made it clear they don't seem open to the idea of Aiyuk playing for San Francisco again.

Lynch told reporters in January it was "safe to assume" had already played his final game with the 49ers. Shanahan said in September, when their injuries were starting to pile up at the receiver position, he would not consider Aiyuk to fill an opening.

It has been more than two full years since Aiyuk last played in an NFL game. He tore the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee during a 28-18 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Oct. 18, 2024.

Aiyuk signed a four-year, $120 million extension with the 49ers in August 2024. He was coming off the best season of his career with 1,342 receiving yards and seven touchdowns in 2023 to help San Francisco reach the Super Bowl.

articles.title: Travis Kelce's sweet reaction to Kylie Kelce's Eagles loyalty reveals the special bond behind their football rivalry
articles.summary: Travis Kelce knows that his sister-in-law, Kylie Kelce, will never put family ties ahead of her love for the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body: Travis Kelce knows that his sister-in-law, Kylie Kelce, will never put family ties ahead of her love for the Philadelphia Eagles. The Kansas City Chiefs star recently praised her honesty on New Heights, joking that Kylie would have no problem telling him to his face that she wanted the Eagles to win, even if it meant cheering against him. Her loyalty is something Travis says he genuinely respects.Travis Kelce appreciates Kylie Kelce’s loyalty to the Philadelphia Eagles despite his Chiefs connectionThe conversation took place during the November 4 episode of New Heights, which Travis hosts with his older brother, Jason Kelce. The brothers were discussing the Kansas City Chiefs’ upcoming game against the New York Jets when longtime show staffer Jake Chatzky found himself caught between his childhood team and his boss. Travis used the exchange to explain why he appreciates Kylie’s straightforward approach to football.Jason asked Chatzky which side he would support when the Jets and Chiefs met on Sunday. Since Chatzky grew up supporting New York, the question put him in an awkward position. He initially hesitated before saying, “I’m absolutely rooting for Travis, for sure, I am 100% rooting for Travis.”Travis was quick to question his answer. Laughing at his colleague, he told him, “You hear that Jets fans? He’s a f***ing phony. He’s a phony.”Chatzky then tried to explain that he was supporting Travis personally rather than openly picking the Chiefs to win. However, Travis was not convinced and replied, “Don’t f***ing lie to my face.”The playful argument gave Travis a reason to bring Kylie into the conversation. Unlike Chatzky, she has never tried to hide which team she wants to win, even when her brother-in-law is playing for the opposition.“At least my sister-in-law will tell me to my face, ‘F*** you, I hope the Birds win,’” Travis said, making Jason and Chatzky laugh.His comment was not meant as criticism. Instead, it showed that Travis knows exactly where Kylie stands and would rather hear her honest opinion than receive support that she does not genuinely feel.Kylie Kelce refuses to wear Kansas City Chiefs gear despite supporting Travis KelceKylie’s loyalty to the Philadelphia Eagles is not something she has started showing recently. She has supported the team since childhood, and her connection to Philadelphia has remained strong even after marrying former Eagles center Jason Kelce.Her decision not to wear Chiefs merchandise became especially noticeable during Super Bowl LVIII in February 2024. The game brought the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers together, giving Kylie a chance to support Travis on one of the biggest nights of his career. However, she still refused to wear an official Chiefs shirt.Instead, Kylie attended the game in a red University of Cincinnati T-shirt, representing the college both Kelce brothers attended. She also wore an “Alright Nah” T-shirt underneath, a small nod to Travis and his familiar expression.Jason had explained the situation during an earlier New Heights episode, revealing that he had tried to convince his wife to make an exception because Travis was playing. He said, “I have tried saying, ‘Kylie, we have family in the game, it’s okay to cheer on that team. They’re not playing the Eagles. You realize this isn’t against the Eagles right?’ She just refuses.”Jason also mentioned that Eagles supporters appreciated her decision to stick with her team despite her family connection to Kansas City.Travis, meanwhile, had no problem with her choice. Even at the time, he made it clear that he valued her presence more than what she wore to the game.“I respect it Ky,” he said. “I appreciate you even wearing red. You could have worn something neutral and just showed your support. You showing up was enough for me, so I appreciate it.”His latest comments show that the understanding has not changed. Kylie can cheer for Philadelphia, Travis can play for Kansas City, and neither has to pretend otherwise to keep their family bond strong.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Calvin Ridley, Titans' Asking Price After Jeffery Simmons Deal
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans are expected to look for a "quality Day 3 pick" in exchange for trading veteran wide receiver Calvin Ridley, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans are expected to look for a "quality Day 3 pick" in exchange for trading veteran wide receiver Calvin Ridley, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday.

According to Fowler, Ridley is "considered a backup plan for a few teams in the receiver market."

Fowler noted, however, the $13 million in cash remaining on Ridley's contract "could be a hurdle" to completing a trade.

The Kansas City Chiefs, Pittsburgh Steelers and Washington Commands have been connected to a search for a wide receiver ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

Other receiving options could be significantly more expensive given that NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the Indianapolis Colts are seeking a third-round pick for Josh Downs.

The news comes after the Titans started selling ahead of the deadline by dealing star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for a package including two first-round picks.

The Titans have since fallen to 1-7 on the season with an overtime loss last Sunday to the Cincinnati Bengals.

Ridley made one catch for 10 yards in the loss, continuing a pattern of low usage that has extended throughout the season.

The wideout has made just six catches for 91 yards in seven games of his third season with the Titans while receiving 13 targets and playing 53 percent of the team's offensive snaps.

Considered a candidate to be released after an injury-limited 2025 season, Ridley stuck around in Nashville after restructuring his contract ahead of the 2026 campaign.

Ridley would likely be a candidate for another restructure or cut with his next team. He is currently signed through 2027 at a $29.75 cap hit, but none of that money is guaranteed until his $2 million roster bonus due in March, per Over the Cap .

Any team targeting Ridley at the deadline would hope in the short term slotting him into a different offensive scheme could help him increase his production down the stretch of his age-32 campaign.

articles.title: Browns place Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol, unclear if Shedeur Sanders will start Week 9
articles.summary: Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit during Sunday's loss to the Steelers.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol, the team announced on Wednesday .

According to the Browns, Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit during the first quarter of Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. The concussion spotter notified the sideline to have the quarterback evaluated. The Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant cleared Watson to return to the game after he missed four snaps.

As part of protocol, Watson was evaluated again after the game, as well as on Monday morning. The Browns say he showed no symptoms and was cleared. But on Tuesday morning he told the team's medical staff that he started experiencing concussion symptoms and was placed into concussion protocol.

Watson threw for 324 yards in the 27-6 loss to the Steelers, but was also sacked eight times. He leads all NFL quarterbacks having been sacked 33 times this season.

There currently is no timeline for a return. The Browns play the New Orleans Saints on Sunday and if Watson cannot play, Shedeur Sanders would likely get the start.

Sanders, who has not started a game since Week 18 last season, made his second appearance of the season coming in briefly for Watson against the Steelers. He went 2-for-2 with 2 passing yards before being replaced. He previously entered in Week 3 and threw one pass for a completion against the Carolina Panthers.

articles.title: Latest on Shedeur Sanders as QB1 with Deshaun Watson Injured in Concussion Protocol for Browns
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders is next in line to start Sunday against the New Orleans Saints after Deshaun Watson was placed into concussion protocol.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders is next in line to start Sunday against the New Orleans Saints after Deshaun Watson was placed into concussion protocol.

Watson experienced symptoms the day after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the team announced Wednesday.

The Browns said Watson was evaluated and cleared by an independent consultant after initially taking the hit in the first quarter of the 27-6 loss in Pittsburgh.

Watson experienced concussion symptoms Monday night and reported them to the team Tuesday morning, according to the Browns.

Sanders is the next man up in Cleveland, with Dillon Gabriel on track to serve as backup, if Watson is not cleared by Sunday.

Watson, who hadn't seen NFL action to 2024 prior to this fall, started all eight games for the Browns this season after winning the QB1 job over Sanders during the preseason.

He has since led the Browns to a 5-3 start that has kept the team in the running to make it out of the AFC North behind the Steelers (6-2) and Cincinnati Bengals (5-2).

Watson most recently threw for a season-high 324 passing yards but was sacked eight times in the loss to the Steelers. He currently leads the league with 33 sacks this season.

Sanders briefly entered the Week 8 matchup while Watson was being following the hit from the Steelers' Jaquan Brisker on the game's opening drive. He completed two passes before Harold Fannin Jr. lost a fumble to end the possession.

The Browns turned to Sanders in Week 11 of his rookie campaign after first starting Kirk Cousins and Dillon Gabriel. He led the Browns to three of their five wins last season and finished the run having completed 56.6 percent of his passes for 1,400 yards with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.

Sanders could look to once more challenge Watson for the starting spot if he gets another chance to work with the Browns' strong receiving core against a Saints passing defense ranked among the bottom 10 in the NFL.

There is still a chance Watson could be cleared to play Sunday. The Browns have placed multiple players including KC Concepcion , Grant Delpit and Tytus Howard in concussion protocol only to clear them to play for a game days later.

Howard was most recently placed in concussion protocol after exiting a Week 7 game, then missed all practices leading up to Week 8 before he was cleared to play against the Steelers.

Whether Watson follows a similar trajectory could determine if Sanders gets his first shot at starting since Week 18 of last season when Sunday's matchup kicks off at 1 p.m. ET in New Orleans.

articles.title: NFL Insider Floats Derrick Henry As Potential Trade Target at Deadline Amid Lamar Jackson Injury
articles.summary: ESPN NFL insider Dan Graziano named Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry as a name to watch ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
ESPN NFL insider Dan Graziano named Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry as a name to watch ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.

Graziano noted that while he is "not sure how realistic" a Henry trade is, it is something the Ravens could consider should they fall to 4-5 on the season with the loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night.

The Ravens placed superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson on injured reserve this week with a thumb injury that required surgery, and head coach Jesse Minter said it could "potentially" keep him out for the rest of the season.

It was also reported by ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport on Wednesday that backup quarterback Tyler Huntley will miss the rest of the 2026 season with turf toe, meaning Baltimore will turn to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano at quarterback this Thursday.

Of course, the Ravens could try to remain in the playoff hunt by adding at the trade deadline and picking up a quarterback, but they could also go in the other direction, and Henry would be a massive trade chip if they do.

Graziano noted that Henry has a base salary of only $1.255 million this season, as the Ravens already paid him $14 million in bonuses. That means it would be easy for another team to take on his contract.

Set to turn 33 on Jan. 4, Henry is signed through next season, although his $12 million salary is not guaranteed.

A five-time Pro Bowler and one-time First Team All-Pro, Henry is widely regarded as one of the greatest running backs of all time and a likely future Hall of Famer.

Henry averaged over 5.0 yards per carry in his first two seasons with the Ravens, and although that number has dipped to 4.0 yards per carry this season, he has still been effective in the form of rushing for 632 yards and eight touchdowns, while also catching 12 passes for 75 yards and a score.

He has been at his best this season with a healthy Jackson under center, as Henry rushed for 374 yards and seven touchdowns over the first four games before Jackson missed three contests with an ankle injury.

A contending team with a solid passing game who needs help at running back could make sense as a destination for Henry with the likes of the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks standing out as potential options.

There is no guarantee the Ravens will look to move on from Henry, especially since he is under contract next season, but he could be a possible game-changer should Baltimore decide to test the trade market.

articles.title: NFL Trade Rumors on Jonathan Taylor, Josh Sweat and More and Latest Predictions
articles.summary: The clock is ticking for NFL teams to make their moves ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.
articles.body:
The clock is ticking for NFL teams to make their moves ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.

A few have already secured significant splashes. The Seattle Seahawks fortified their offensive line with Quenton Nelson. The San Francisco 49ers and Chicago Bears, meanwhile, beefed up their defensive tackle spots with DeForest Buckner and Jeffery Simmons, respectively.

Will those acquisitions wind up being the most impactful moves of this trade season? Or could other clubs have some cannonball-sized splashes of their own up their sleeve? Let's run through the latest rumor-mill rumblings to find out.

Teams in the market for pass-rushers just received a welcome update. Arizona Cardinals impact edge-rusher Josh Sweat would apparently welcome a deadline relocation, per NFL insider Jordan Schultz.

Now, the note about Sweat feeling this way since the offseason seems...well, notable. As does Arizona's apparent "high" asking price.

Still, if shoppers need an incentive to cover a high cost for Sweat, his track record could give them that. He has twice delivered double-digit sack totals, including last season, when he had a career-high 12 sacks to go along with 17 quarterback hits. His three sacks this season have all come within the last five games, too, so he might be rounding into form.

That doesn't mean Arizona will definitely grant his wish, especially if the Cardinals think they might catch lightning in a bottle with Garnder Minshew II. Still, they're stuck at the bottom of a strong NFC West, so their future likely outweighs their present in terms of importance.

Prediction: Sweat is traded to the Dallas Cowboys.

Colts Setting Steep Price for Jonathan Taylor?

With Buckner and Nelson both out of the Circle City, it sure seems like the Indianapolis Colts are in tear-down mode. And while they seem likely to remain busy leading up to the deadline, it's still unclear if star running back Jonathan Taylor will be among the subtractions.

The Colts are "asking for a lot" for Taylor and "taking the stance that they don't need to move him," per ESPN's Dan Graziano . The report opined that "enough teams are interested in Taylor that it's too soon for the Colts to think about lowering their demands."

So, what would it take to get a deal done? ESPN's Jeremy Fowler added in the same piece that rival executives pegged Taylor's worth as "a second-round pick plus an additional pick" while noting the Colts "could be holding out for the equivalent of a first-round pick."

The list of possible landing spots for Taylor is not short, as several teams with playoff aspirations could stand to upgrade at the position. Taylor, a three-time Pro Bowl honoree who has tallied 812 scrimmage yards and eight touchdowns in eight games this season, would absolutely qualify as such.

Prediction: Taylor is traded to the New York Giants.

Regardless if Jonathan Taylor is moved, it's hard to imagine Indy is done dealing . Josh Downs feels like one of the more logical trade candidates on the roster, in part because he has already asked out .

His age (25) and ability (30 catches for 330 yards and a score) should strike the right combo to drum up interest. The fact he is eligible for free agency at season's end could lead to the Colts deeming him expendable.

He is reportedly "of interest to the Steelers and the Chiefs," per Graziano. Given how many win-now shoppers could use more receiving help, Downs' list of landing spots surely runs longer than that.

Downs would fit well in either Pittsburgh or Kansas City. He'd be a good get in Washington, too. San Francisco has obvious (and immediate) needs in its receiving group. A reunion in New England with quarterback Drake Maye would make sense. So would helping the Los Angeles Rams fill the Davante Adams void. You get the idea.

Prediction: Downs is traded to the Pittsburgh Steeers.

articles.summary: Having already tried to go big before the trade deadline by inquiring about Jeffery Simmons, the New York Giants are still looking to take a home-run swing to improve the interior of their defensive line.

Having already tried to go big before the trade deadline by inquiring about Jeffery Simmons, the New York Giants are still looking to take a home-run swing to improve the interior of their defensive line.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Tampa Bay Buccaneers star Vita Vea is on the "radar" for the Giants leading up to the Nov. 10 deadline.

Before Simmons was traded to the Chicago Bears last week, Giants head coach John Harbuagh reportedly made a direct call to Tennessee Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk in an attempt to deal for the four-time Pro Bowler.

Vea would certainly be an incredible fallback plan for the Giants, but the Bucs' turnaround following their 0-4 start would seemingly make it unlikely they even entertain a trade offer for him.

Fowler noted the Buccaneers are not expected to move Vea. It's not a bad idea to at least try to gauge Tampa's interest after Vea had a contract standoff with the club during the offseason before the two sides agreed to a one-year, $30 million extension in August. He will be 32 next season with a $30.6 million cap hit in 2027.

The Bucs have won three of their last four games, including back-to-back wins over divisional opponents in the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons. They are only one game back in the loss column of Carolina for first place in the NFC South.

New York's desire to be aggressive speaks to the fact this team looks to be ahead of schedule right now and the rest of the NFC East being a disaster. The Giants are the only team in the division with a winning record and are unbeaten in two divisional games thus far.

It does perhaps sting that the Giants are looking for an interior defensive lineman after trading Dexter Lawrence to the Cincinnati Bengals in the offseason, but they are set up well to potentially make the playoffs in Harbaugh's first season as head coach.

The Giants have already won as many games this season as they did in all of 2025. One more victory will give them their highest single-season win total since finishing 6-11 in 2023.

articles.title: How Travis Kelce went from a $995,000 Kansas City home to building a multimillion-dollar real estate portfolio
articles.summary: Travis Kelce's success in the NFL has brought him more than championship rings, lucrative contracts and national fame.
articles.body: Travis Kelce's success in the NFL has brought him more than championship rings, lucrative contracts and national fame. It has also changed the way he invests in real estate. The Kansas City Chiefs star began his property journey with a home worth less than $1 million. Years later, he was making multimillion-dollar purchases in some of the country's most exclusive neighbourhoods. His latest Ohio acquisition adds another chapter to that story, taking his reported property purchases to more than $12 million.Travis Kelce started his real estate journey with a $995,000 Kansas City homeBefore luxury estates and multimillion-dollar property deals became part of his lifestyle, Kelce made a relatively modest entry into the Kansas City housing market.In 2019, the tight end purchased a property in the Briarcliff West neighbourhood for approximately $995,000. At the time, he was already an established name with the Chiefs, but his property choice reflected a different stage of his career.The house was hardly an ordinary starter home. Reports described a roughly 10,000-square-foot residence with seven bedrooms and five bathrooms. It also featured a gourmet kitchen, an indoor gym, a wine cellar and a built-in bar. Outside, a swimming pool and gazebo provided plenty of space to relax.The property offered the NFL star privacy and comfort without the scale of the estates he would purchase later.There is also an interesting financial detail. Kelce's first reported home purchase was less than one-sixth of the price of his later Leawood mansion. That difference shows how his real estate choices expanded as his career and earning power developed.However, there is no confirmed public sale price for this first property. It is also unclear whether Kelce still owns it. Therefore, its purchase price should not be treated as a realised investment return.Travis Kelce makes a major upgrade with his $5.99 million Leawood mansionKelce's next major property purchase marked a significant change in scale.In 2023, the Chiefs star purchased a luxury estate in Leawood, Kansas, for approximately $5.99 million. The gated property offered a level of privacy and space that was a considerable step up from his earlier Kansas City residence.Spread across roughly 3.5 acres, the mansion covers around 17,000 square feet. Its features include six bedrooms, six bathrooms, a chef's kitchen, a formal dining room and a media lounge.But the amenities do not stop inside.The outdoor area includes a swimming pool, an outdoor kitchen, tennis and pickleball facilities, a waterfall, a hot tub and even a miniature golf course. The property also has a wine cellar and a full bar, making it suitable for entertaining guests.The estate's location is another major advantage. Its position inside a gated community offers privacy while keeping Kelce within convenient reach of the Chiefs' home stadium.Over time, Kelce has also invested in improvements to the property. Reports in late 2024 revealed plans for an underground man cave, adding another personal touch to the already elaborate residence.The purchase price represented an increase of nearly $5 million over his first reported home acquisition. It also showed that Kelce was willing to spend more on a home that offered security, recreation and room for his growing personal life.Travis Kelce adds a $5.35 million Ohio mansion to his property portfolioJust when his Kansas and Missouri property connections seemed substantial, Kelce made another major real estate move in 2026.The NFL star purchased a historic lakefront estate in Bratenahl, Ohio, for $5.35 million. The property sits on approximately 3.5 acres along Lake Erie and is only a short distance from Cleveland Heights, where Kelce grew up.The location makes this purchase particularly interesting. Unlike his Kansas properties, which keep him close to his professional football commitments, the Ohio estate brings him closer to his childhood roots.Known as Moyenage, the mansion dates back to the late 19th century and spans approximately 21,000 square feet. It has eight bedrooms and 11 bathrooms, along with several distinctive features that separate it from a typical luxury residence.The original ballroom has been transformed into a game room and home theatre. The estate also includes a two-bedroom guest cottage created from a former gatehouse.The property underwent extensive restoration before Kelce purchased it. Figurati Construction Group acquired the mansion for $1.95 million in 2023 and carried out renovation work before placing it on the market.Its original asking price reached $6.99 million. The listing was later reduced to $5.99 million, before Kelce completed the purchase for $5.35 million.That means the Chiefs star paid $640,000 less than the property's reduced asking price. Compared with its original listing, the difference was $1.64 million.However, that does not automatically mean the property was undervalued. Its final price reflected the condition, location and negotiations involved in the transaction.The Ohio purchase also adds a personal dimension to Kelce's property decisions. He has maintained a strong connection to the Cleveland area throughout his career, and the estate gives him a substantial home near the place where he grew up.Travis Kelce's property purchases reveal how his lifestyle has evolvedLooking at the three reported acquisitions together reveals an interesting financial progression.Kelce's first reported purchase cost approximately $995,000. His Leawood estate followed at nearly $5.99 million, while the Bratenahl property added another $5.35 million to the total.Combined, those historical purchase prices come to approximately $12.34 million.That is a significant amount, although it should not be confused with the current market value of his properties or his confirmed net worth. The figure also does not account for renovations, maintenance, taxes or other expenses. Public information does not establish whether he continues to own all three homes.His property choices also reflect different priorities. The Briarcliff West home served him during the earlier years of his NFL career. The Leawood mansion offered greater privacy and extensive recreational facilities. The Ohio estate, meanwhile, provides a connection to his hometown and a distinctive lakefront setting.Kelce's growing wealth has also come from opportunities outside football, including endorsements, business partnerships and his New Heights podcast with brother Jason.His real estate moves offer a visible look at that financial journey. Rather than simply choosing increasingly expensive houses, he has acquired properties that serve different purposes at different stages of his life.For Kelce, the journey from a $995,000 Kansas City home to a $5.35 million Ohio estate is about more than luxury. It reflects a career that has created opportunities well beyond the football field, while allowing him to maintain connections to both his professional home and his childhood roots.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Voter whose Form 6 was rejected questions EC after fresh re-enrolment clarification
articles.summary: Election Commission clarifies voters deleted during SIR can seek re-inclusion via Form 6, prompting a Bengal elector whose earlier Form 6 was rejected to question EC.
articles.body: Kolkata: Election Commission’s decision to allow Form 6 for re-enrolment of voters deleted during SIR has led a 62-year-old man, who had taken the same route before Bengal Assembly polls, to question who should be held responsible for taking away his right to vote.Hasir Mallick, a resident of Uttarpara, had his name struck off the rolls when the post-SIR roll was published in Feb. He had earlier appeared for hearings after his name was flagged for “logical discrepancy”. Advised by some acquaintances, Mallick filed a Form 6 online.Form 6 is meant for enrolment of new voters. It is meant for those who attain the age of 18 or are applying for enrolment for the first time.“Names of my son and wife were in the roll and my name had been removed. I filed a Form 6 online. I received a message asking me to appear at the office of SDO, Serampore. There the officials told me that I cannot file Form 6 as I was not a new voter and my name had been deleted,” Mallick told TOI. Later, Mallick received a message that his application had been rejected.He later filed an appeal with the SIR tribunals, a decision on which is still pending. “I do not know whether I will be able to vote in the next elections also. My son’s passport is due for renewal next year. I am now worried whether his passport will be rejected because his father’s name does not feature on the voters’ list,” said Mallick.Nearly seven months since his application was rejected, Election Commission said on Tuesday that voters deleted from draft SIR rolls may seek re-inclusion by filing Form 6. “EC should have announced its decision much earlier,” he said. “I also need to know whether I can file a Form 6 now as my name was missing from the final roll and I have also appealed to the tribunals,” he asked.Election Commission on Tuesday clarified that no action will be taken against a previous elector whose name is deleted from draft rolls published during SIR and who seeks re-inclusion by filling in Form 6. In a communication to CEOs of all states and Union Territories on Tuesday, EC said voters who are not registered in another constituency can file Form 6 for re-enrolment if their names were missing from draft SIR rolls.Recalling a Delhi HC order dated Oct 14 that held as “misplaced” the apprehension of an applicant, who argued that submitting Form 6 would amount to making a false declaration, EC directed that “no action shall be initiated under Section 31 of the R P Act by an ERO against an elector merely on the ground that the elector had been included in a previous electoral roll and has submitted Form 6 during the SIR process or afterwards, provided the elector is not already enrolled in any other parliamentary or assembly constituency and the declaration made is otherwise in accordance with law”.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Brian Kelly’s Florida State interest raises new questions after Urban Meyer highlights Mike Norvell’s $50.3 million buyout
articles.summary: Urban Meyer has raised serious questions about Florida State’s ability to afford its next head coach after the university fired Mike Norvell.
articles.body: Urban Meyer has raised serious questions about Florida State’s ability to afford its next head coach after the university fired Mike Norvell. The former Ohio State coach is concerned about the program’s financial position, especially with Norvell’s reported $50.3 million buyout. Meanwhile, former LSU coach Brian Kelly has expressed interest in the vacant job, adding another name to the growing coaching discussion.Urban Meyer raises major Florida state concerns after Mike Norvell’s $50.3 million buyoutFlorida State’s decision to move on from Mike Norvell has created a difficult situation for the university. The Seminoles fired him on November 1 after an unsuccessful 3-5 start to the 2026 season. He finished his time in Tallahassee with a 41-39 record across six-plus seasons, despite previously leading the team to an undefeated 13-0 regular season in 2023.Speaking on the Triple Option podcast on November 3, Urban Meyer questioned how the university would manage the financial pressure. He also referred to comments made by Florida State president Richard McCullough about the school’s financial position.“The president, I watched the interview today because I was interested. He sounds like a guy, I mean, the financial restraints. I know they’ll find the money, but as of now, that place is in financial ruins,” Meyer said.The biggest concern is Norvell’s contract. According to On3, his buyout is around $50.3 million following his midseason dismissal. Florida State also has to deal with the cost of parting ways with other members of the coaching staff and bringing in replacements. On3 sources have estimated that firing the staff and hiring a new head coach could push the overall expense towards $100 million.Florida State’s existing financial position makes that decision even harder. According to On3, which cited Sportico’s Daniel Libit, the university reported $437 million in athletics-related debt for fiscal year 2025. Much of that amount is connected to the renovation of Doak Campbell Stadium and the construction of a new football operations centre.Meyer also questioned whether Florida State should spend another huge amount on an established coach.“To hire new staff, buyouts, paying off the coaching staff, and hire a quality new head coach with the market it is, I’m curious. I love Mike Norvell; he’s going to be fine. But what the h*** do they do at Florida State?” he added.Instead, Meyer pointed towards coaches such as Curt Cignetti and Bob Chesney, who built their reputations outside the biggest college football programs before moving to major jobs.“The table’s been set with Bob Chesney and Curt Cignetti, and you can get them cheap,” Meyer said, suggesting that Florida State could consider a less expensive coaching option.Brian Kelly expresses interest in Florida State job after Mike Norvell’s firingWhile Meyer believes Florida State should be careful with its next coaching decision, Brian Kelly has already shown interest in the opportunity. The former Notre Dame and LSU coach discussed the vacancy during an appearance on SiriusXM’s College Sports Radio on November 3.Kelly admitted that an unemployed coach might welcome almost any opportunity, but he also spoke positively about Florida State’s history and fan base.“When you’re talking to an unemployed football coach, every job’s a great job, you know? But Florida State, look, I’ve got a great history with Florida State, great games,” Kelly said.He also added that leading the Seminoles would be “an honor and privilege.”Kelly brings plenty of experience, having coached at Central Michigan, Cincinnati, Notre Dame and LSU. His LSU team finished with a 34-14 record before the university dismissed him during the 2025 season. However, his previous LSU contract also came with a reported buyout of more than $50 million, which raises another financial question for Florida State.There is also a leadership issue at the university. Florida State dismissed athletic director Michael Alford in September, leaving president Richard McCullough and interim athletic director Bruce Warwick to oversee the transition. Rick Stockstill has been named interim head coach while the Seminoles look for Norvell’s replacement.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Former Chicago Bears All-Pro offensive lineman Kyle Long noticed something interesting during ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcast of the Bears and Seattle...
articles.body:
Former Chicago Bears All-Pro offensive lineman Kyle Long noticed something interesting during ESPN's Monday Night Football broadcast of the Bears and Seattle Seahawks.

As Chicago cruised to a 34-17 road victory, Long took to X with a short message about play-by-play announcer Joe Buck and analyst Troy Aikman. His observation caught the attention of NFL fans, particularly those who have followed Aikman's history with the Bears' quarterback, Caleb Williams.

From Past Criticism to Praise for Caleb Williams

"Joe Buck teeing up Troy Aikman to say nice things about Caleb Williams is must listen," Long wrote .

The former Bears lineman's 16-word message highlighted a noticeable change in the broadcast, with Aikman offering plenty of praise for Williams during the game.

The third-year quarterback delivered a strong performance against Seattle, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and a touchdown. Williams also has earned an 84.0 grade in PFN's NFL QB Impact Metric , ranking sixth among quarterbacks.

Aikman's positive comments stood out because of his previous criticism of Williams during a late-2025 Monday Night Football broadcast against the Washington Commanders.

During that game, Aikman described one of Williams' touchdown passes as "lucky" and questioned aspects of his decision-making. The comments drew criticism from Bears fans.

Williams later mentioned that he had not participated in a pregame production meeting with Aikman. The former Cowboys quarterback, meanwhile, defended his remarks as fair and unbiased analysis while maintaining that he was impressed by Williams' overall talent before praising his performance against Seattle.

Joe Buck and Troy Aikman's Broadcast Future Remains a Talking Point

Long's post also came amid ongoing discussions about Buck and Aikman's future together at ESPN.

The broadcasting duo has worked together for 25 years, dating back to their time at Fox. However, their contract situations have recently attracted attention.

Buck reportedly signed a six-year, $108 million extension with ESPN, while Aikman is entering the final year of his five-year, $90 million deal, which expires in February 2027.

Aikman was reportedly caught off guard when he learned that Buck had finalized his new contract without telling him. The situation reportedly led to disagreements between the two ahead of an October game between the Buffalo Bills and the Los Angeles Rams.

Aikman has publicly acknowledged that he will enter free agency after the season, raising questions about his future in broadcasting.

Despite the uncertainty, Buck and Aikman are expected to finish the season together, with ESPN preparing for its first-ever Super Bowl broadcast on February 14, 2027.

articles.title: Chiefs Could Swing for Texans’ Former First-Round Pick to Fix Glaring Issues
articles.summary: The Houston Texans are 2-5. They opened their 25th season with Super Bowl hopes but lost their first four games. The defense has slipped. Houston allowed 17....
articles.body:
The Houston Texans are 2-5. They opened their 25th season with Super Bowl hopes but lost their first four games.

The defense has slipped. Houston allowed 17.4 points per game last season, second in the NFL. This season, it allows 24.3, which ranks 19th.

The Texans led the NFL in yards allowed last season at 277.2 per game. They now rank 18th at 342 per game.

On the other hand, the Kansas City Chiefs are 5-2. They are managing quite well, but a certain Texans player could add to their performance

Chiefs to Pursue Texans' Former First-Round Pick

Kansas City could trade for Jadeveon Clowney in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick.

They need help rushing the passer. The Chiefs pressured Denver quarterback Bo Nix on 2 of 34 dropbacks in Week 8. That equals a 6% pressure rate in a 28-24 loss.

No NFL team had posted a lower rate in a game since Week 5 of 2024.

They also want a receiver. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported last week that the Chiefs appear poised to add one because of injuries to receivers Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton.

Clowney fits as a trade chip for a 2-5 team. His one-year deal expires after this season, so Houston would give up no long-term asset.

The Texans also have depth at defensive end. Clowney supplements stars Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson Jr.

Clowney, 33, agreed to a one-year contract with Houston on Aug. 2. It is worth $5.5 million, with incentives that can raise it to $8 million.

The Texans drafted him No. 1 overall in 2014. He spent his first five seasons in Houston.

A deal is plausible on price. Houston's stance and Kansas City's cap are the bigger hurdles.

Houston has not committed to selling. General manager Nick Caserio said Oct. 26 that the Texans plan no significant personnel changes. They also gain little financially.

Clowney has drawn other suitors before. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Nov. 1 that Clowney has generated some interest, but no team was mentioned.

Kansas City faces its own limits. The Chiefs had roughly $3 million in cap space at their Week 5 bye. That figure is dated. Clowney's base salary is $2.5 million. The Chiefs would owe the prorated remainder.

Clowney is a rotational rusher, so the Chiefs would be buying depth rather than a star.

articles.title: Receiver Brandon Aiyuk files paperwork to be reinstated to the 49ers
articles.summary: (AP) — Receiver Brandon Aiyuk has applied to be reinstated to the San Francisco 49ers from the reserve/left squad list and plans to report to the team later...
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. (AP) — Receiver Brandon Aiyuk has applied to be reinstated to the San Francisco 49ers from the reserve/left squad list and plans to report to the team later this week.

Aiyuk's new agent, Drew Rosenhaus , said Wednesday that Aiyuk has officially submitted his paperwork to the NFL to get back and is planning to return to the 49ers on Friday.

Aiyuk hasn't played a game in more than two years since going down with a knee injury in October 2024 and has been on the reserve/left squad list after leaving the Niners late last season.

He fired agent Ryan Williams during his long-running dispute with the 49ers and was without representation until he recently hired Rosenhaus.

Aiyuk will remain under contract with the 49ers after he is reinstated by the NFL. San Francisco general manager John Lynch previously has said he doesn't expect Aiyuk to play for the Niners again.

They previously voided $27 million guaranteed in Aiyuk's contract for 2026 for failing to participate in meetings and other team activities last summer when he was rehabilitating his knee injury.

Aiyuk signed a four-year, $120 million extension just before the start of the 2024 season following a lengthy contract hold-in that kept him out of training camp. He was coming off a 2023 season when he had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns and was a second-team All-Pro.

Aiyuk had only 25 catches for 374 yards in seven games in 2024 before getting injured. The 28-year-old has 294 catches for 4,305 yards and 25 TDs since being drafted in the first round in 2020.

articles.title: Eagles on pace for worst offense since 1998: How did it get to this point?
articles.summary: The Eagles have their worst offense through eight games this century. What were the factors that got them to this stage?
articles.body:
There's no argument the Philadelphia Eagles offense is bad. The 2026 unit is historically bad.

The Eagles are 29th in the NFL in points per game (17.1) and 30th in points per drive (1.61). They're 32nd in yards per game (265.3) and yards per play (4.4), far from the offensive juggernauts the franchise has posted this century — whether that would be from Andy Reid, Chip Kelly, Doug Pederson, or even Nick Sirianni.

There has only been one Eagles team that has put up fewer points than the 2026 squad this century. The 2012 Eagles averaged just 16.6 points per game, and they ended up with a 4-12 record in what would be Reid's last season. The 1.61 points per possession is also the lowest since 2012.

The 265.3 yards per game is the lowest through eight games since 1999 (244.0), and that Eagles team started 1-7 before rallying to finish 5-11 (year one under Reid). The 4.42 yards per play is the lowest since 1999 (3.92), and only the 1998 offense was worse than those two (3.73).

Those 1998 Eagles were an abomination. They were 30th out of 30 teams in points per game (10.1) and yards per game (261.7). That was the only time in franchise history the Eagles finished in the 30s in points and yards per game. If points per possession and yards per possession were measured in 1998, the Eagles would have been last in those categories too.

The 2026 Eagles have the worst offense this century, and is the worst Eagles offense since 1998. That unit had Bobby Hoying start the seaosn before a rotating carousel of quarterbacks that included Rodney Peete and Koy Detmer. The Eagles went from Hoying to Peete before returning to Hoying and eventually Detmer.

So how did the 2026 Eagles get to this point? How did they go from a top-10 offense, to middle of the back, to what they are now — all over the past year?

There were quite a few contributing factors towards the Eagles offense reaching historically bad levels for the franchise.

1. Jeff Stoutland deciding not to return

The Eagles offensive line was middle of the pack last season, the first time in the Nick Sirianni era the offensive line wasn't a top-10 unit. Outside of Lane Johnson, all the other starters on the offensive line started 14+ games — so injuries didn't play a factor in the mediocrity.

Stoutland's role as run-game coordinator also regressed, as Nick Sirianni and former offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo began incorporating different run designs to the offense. With these changes in place, Stoutland reportedly wasn't consulted about them as his title was in name only.

With Stoutland not having a prominent voice as in years past, he decided to step aside after the 2025 season. Chris Kuper was hired as the offensive line coach, despite the Minnesota Vikings ranking 31st in sack rate (11.0%) and 27th in pressure rate allowed per dropback (39.8%) last season. The Vikings were 26th in sack rate (8.0%) and 29th in pressure rate (37.8%) from 2022 to 2025 under Kuper.

The Eagles offensive line under Kuper this year? They are 24th in sack rate (7.9%) and 28th in pressure rate (42.7%). They were 19th in sack rate (6.7%) and 20th in pressure rate (35.4%) last year.

2. The Kevin Patullo hire, followed by Sean Mannion hire

The Eagles were coming off a Super Bowl victory in the 2024 season, but offensive coordinator Kellen Moore was leaving after one season to take the New Orleans Saints head coaching job. Philadelphia didn't have a deep opol of candidates for the offensive coordinator role since the Eagles played into February, so Patullo was promoted from passing game coordinator to offensive coordinator.

Patullo was passing game coordinator for four seasons, and came over from the Indianapolis Colts with Nick Sirianni. His lone season as offensive coordinator was a disaster, as the scoring dropped from 27.2 points per game to 22.3 (seventh to 19th) and points per possession from 2.50 to 2.00 (eighth to 21st). Yards per game dropped from 367.2 to 3111.2 (seventh to 24th) and yards per play from 5.6 to 5.2 (11th to 19th). The Eagles went from 24.7% in three-and-out rate to 36.0% (21st to fourth).

The offense got worse with Sean Mannion hired to replace Patullo, as the changes to the offensive scheme has made the unit worst. Injuries to the offense haven't helped (Jordan Mailata is the only player to start every game), but the Eagles are historically bad on offense.

To showcase Mannion's struggles, look at the second half of games.The Eagles average 4.6 points per game and 3.9 yards per play (both 32nd in the NFL). The third quarter is even worse, ranking 32nd in points per game (1.6), yards per game (43.0), yards per carry (2.5), yards per play (3.1), and yards per attempt (4.0).

Johnson's sudden retirement played a factor in how this offense has performed, as the Eagles haven't won a game since his sudden retirement after Week 4. The Eagles are 0-3 since Johnson retired, and 3-8 in games he's missed since last season (including playoffs).

The Eagles were 122-63-1 with Johnson in the lineup, a .659 win percentage (including postseason). They are 18-30 without him, a .375 win percentage.

Johnson's replacement at right tackle, Markel Bell, has had a rough start to his career. Bell has allowed five sacks in his three starts, and is tied for second amongst right tackles in most sacks allowed. He has allowed a 7.3% pressure rate per dropback this season — seventh-worst amongst right tackles in the NFL.

Right tackle is a new position for Bell, and he wasn't expected to play this year. Bell was expected to take over for Johnson after this season, just three years after moving up to FBS from Holmes Community College.

The Eagles were going to have to adjust to life without Johnson at some point. This wasn't expected to happen this season.

Any time a team loses their franchise quarterback hurts. What Jalen Hurts over the past month is way bigge rthan football.

Hurts was discovered to have a having a superficial blood clot in his leg following the team's trip to London, which was discovered before he played in the team's Week 5 game against the Jaguars. An ultrasound in the middle of that week found the blood clot had moved to his lungs, which put Hurts on blood thinners and ruled him out for the season.

The Eagles are 58-25 in games Hurts has started since he became the full-time starting quarterback in 2021, a .699 win percentage. Without Hurts, the Eagles are 3-7 in 10 games — a .300 win percentage.

The Eagles passing game has struggled with Hurts, but he has found ways to win football games. They just aren't getting that when Hurts isn't on the field.

In the three games Tanner McKee has started, the Eagles are 32nd in yards per play (4.2), 31st in yards per attempt (5.6), and 29th in offensive points per game (15.0). McKee has completed 63.2% of his passes for 638 yards with 2 TD, 2 INT, and a 76.6 passer rating. He is 31st out of 32 qualified quarterbacks in yards per attempt (5.6) and 26th in passer rating.

There is a massive drop off from Hurts to McKee, who couldn't beat out Andy Dalton for the QB2 job this summer.

The Eagles didn't have the depth at tight end in the 2025 season, despite Dallas Goedert having 11 touchdown catches. Goedert had 591 receiving yards and the rest of the tight ends had a combined 116. While the Eagles ranked 22nd in tight end receiving yards, they also had a significant hole in blocking at the position.

The Eagles addressed the position by signing Johnny Mundt to a one-year contract as teh blocking tight end and drafting Eli Stowers in the second round to be the TE2 behind Goedert. Stowers struggled to gain separation from defenders in minicamp, which moved over to training camp before missing the first six games with hamstring and quad injuries.

Mundt has struggled as a blocker while being the de facto TE2. A Grant Calcaterra injury at the end of training camp didn't help matters either. Once Goedert missed time with a knee injury, the Eagles had to sign 36-year-old Zach Ertz just to have a pass catcher at teh position.

Ertz can't get elevated to the active roster, Mundt is struggling in the offense, and Stowers has just two games into his career. Stowers had 46 yards in garbage time in Sunday's loss to Washington, placing him second on the team in receiving yards for the tight end position.

Goedert has 258 receiving yards and the reminder of the Eagles tight ends have a combined 91. The Eagles are 17th in the NFL in receiving yards amongst tight ends with 349, but also haven't had their bye week yet.

While the position is healthy now, Mannion's offense thrives with two and three tight ends on the field. The Eagles have one capable tight end at this point, which is on the front office for not addressing the position well enough in the offseason.

Perhaps more playing time for Stowers will change that, even if the only time he's been effective is late in games when the outcome has bene determined.

articles.title: George Pickens rumors: Ranking 6 landing spots for Cowboys WR at trade deadline or in free agency
articles.summary: The Cowboys may be moving on from their No. 2 wide receiver, either now or later. Here's a look at his best new team fits.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys decided to pay wide receiver George Pickens on a one-year franchise tag at the cost of $27.298 million for the 2026 NFL season. He's given them little reason to reconsider signing him to a long-term extension.

Pickens remains a pending 2027 NFL free agent. After breaking out with 93 catches for 1,429 receiving yards and nine TDs last season in Dallas after coming over in a trade from Pittsburgh, Pickens has had a big production drop-off through the first half of '26.

Through eight Cowboys games, Pickens has only 39 catches for 533 yards and two TDs. He's on pace for 83 catches for 1,133 yards and four TDs. That's still a pretty good season, but not worth (yet) giving him money close to top wide receiver CeeDee Lamb, who averages $36 million per season on his current four-year, $36 million deal he signed in 2024.

Pickens becoming a free agent without being tagged again has created some rumors of a potential trade now ahead of a likely departure from Dallas next March. But what teams are the best fits to become Pickens' third NFL team, now or later? Here's a ranking of the juiciest suitors. MORE: Why the Cowboys should - and shouldn't - trade George Pickens

George Pickens trade and free agency landing spots, ranked

The Falcons have the best shot at acquiring Pickens before the Nov. 10 in-season trade deadline next Tuesday. They have ample cap space to pay what's left on Pickens' 2026 salary. They also need another downfield passing target to help Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson in the passing game. They are seeing good signs from big-armed third-year QB Michael Penix Jr.

The Falcons, at 3-5, are also in playoff contention in the weak NFC South race. Pickens can help them finish ahead of the Panthers , Buccaneers and Saints in the end. Atlanta has a ton of cap space in the near future to also give Pickens a long-term deal, in which he would earn more than $30 million per season. MORE: The best possible deadline deals for 12 playoff contenders

The Dolphins may not be well positioned to buy at the trade deadline. That means the interest would be in beating other teams to the punch to sign Pickens. The key is the asking price, and Miami likely would be OK only giving up a second-round draft pick to Dallas. When there is no such compensation involved beyond the big money in NFL free agency, the Dolphins make a lot of sense for Pickens to attach to a young franchise QB they take in the first round.

Miami is taking a long look at several young receivers this season with Malik Willis at quarterback, but none of them profile like a No. 1 like Pickens does. MORE: The Sporting News Midseason All-Pro Team

The Rams are seeing the breakdown of Davante Adams ahead of him turning 34 in December, as he is sidelined for up to three months with a hamstring injury. Los Angeles can get out of Adams' contract next year, as he is also a pending free agent.

That would leave Matthew Stafford (likely returning for another season at QB) with a big void for a big playmaker to pair with Puka Nacua, who is up for a big contract extension next year. Given the aggressive nature of their all-in offseason with GM Les Snead, don't put it past the Rams to go after Pickens now should they feel Adams' chances of being effective in a return aren't good.

The trick is how they might pay Nacua and Pickens at the same time. But for a team with still huge Super Bowl 61 hopes, they might be OK with "renting" Pickens for a half-season through the playoffs.

The Raiders are another wide receiver-needy team with Tre Tucker as their best option to help tight end Brock Bowers this season. Although Kirk Cousins is still making it work with his current weapons, the Raiders need to be thinking more about the future with No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza.

It would be shocking if Mendoza isn't the anointed starter in his second season. Las Vegas would be smart to gamble on Pickens' big-play ability connecting well with Mendoza and playing well off Bowers. The Raiders would be more of a free-agent fit, unless John Spytek wants to build on his aggressive 2026 offseason soon. MORE: NFL midseason awards, from "Biggest Disappointment" to "Worst Coaching Decision"

The Cardinals like Michael Wilson as their top wide receiver playing off their star tight end, Trey McBride. But with Jacoby Brissett benched, Gardner Minshew playing the bridge and rookie Carson Beck as the No. 2, Arizona is fast-forwarding a little to the future of Mike LaFleur's offense.

The question is, after the drama with Marvin Harrison Jr., another big speedy wide receiver with inconsistent mercurial tendencies, would the Cardinals want to risk that again and give up big money and draft capital to get Pickens? They will kick his tires should he hit the open market and might think he will come out flat for them in the same way. MORE: Breaking down the Cowboys' defensive disaster

The Commanders have seen Terry McLaurin go down with a devastating injury. They had to sign Stefon Diggs to give themselves some preseason help at wide receiver, but now Diggs has to be the default No. 1 the rest of the way for Jayden Daniels.

Washington is sitting pretty on cap space as Daniels is on his rookie contract. Much like the Falcons, despite a losing record (2-4-1), the Commanders should feel like they can still get into the playoffs through winning their own weak division, the NFC East.

Obviously, a Cowboys-Commanders trade between rivals would be odd, so this would be more about Washington targeting Pickens as a free agent to pair with a (hopefully) back-healthy McLaurin next season.

articles.title: Steelers' Zach Frazier receives legendary comparison to all-time great
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers legendary QB Ben Roethlisberger offered high praise for C Zach Frazier, comparing him to Maurkice Pouncey.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers standout center Zach Frazier has drawn comparisons from Ben Roethlisberger to one of the team's all-time greats.

On a recent episode of the Footbahlin' with Ben Roethlisberger podcast, Big Ben praised Frazier as the cornerstone of Pittsburgh's dominant offensive line in 2026, comparing him to legendary Steelers center Maurkice Pouncey.

"He's the anchor in the middle, he reminds me of Pouncey," Roethlisberger said. "He reminds me of the tough, 'I don't really need anything. I'm just gonna go out and do my job.' ... At some point, he needs to start getting his Pro Bowl nods. ... And then that turns into the All-Pro nods. He's that guy."

10 trade targets for Steelers ahead of 2026 NFL deadline

Frazier, drafted by the Steelers in the second round of the 2024 NFL Draft, has been dominant in 2026, allowing just one quarterback hit and zero sacks, while also recording a solid PFF run-blocking grade of 79.8, third best among all eligible centers.

Frazier would definitely have some big shoes to fill when it comes to Pouncey, who was selected to two first-team All-Pro teams, three second-team All-Pro teams and nine Pro Bowls during his 11-year NFL career with the Steelers.
